short_description.id: Loong adalah naga dalam mitologi Tiongkok, lazim digambarkan menyerupai ular dengan empat kaki.
short_description.en: Loong belongs to Chinese mythology and commonly has a serpentine shape with four legs.

long_description.id:
Loong adalah naga dalam mitologi Tiongkok, lazim digambarkan menyerupai ular dengan empat kaki. Naga menjadi lambang kekuasaan kaisar dalam sejarah Tiongkok.

Bentuk naga melingkar juga ditemukan pada amulet giok zaman Shang. Sebagian benda yang dahulu disebut tulang naga ternyata fosil mamalia. Wang Fu mencatat tradisi sembilan kemiripan anatomi naga dengan hewan lain. Doré mencatat varian anatomi dengan tanduk rusa dan kepala buaya. Naga dalam seni sering mengejar atau memperebutkan mutiara menyala. Kepercayaan populer menghubungkan naga dengan sungai, laut, dan pengaturan hujan. Saat kekeringan atau banjir, masyarakat melakukan ritual untuk memohon bantuan raja naga setempat. Sebuah legenda mengisahkan Kaisar Kuning naik ke langit setelah menjadi naga. Museum Norton menjelaskan naga sebagai penguasa langit yang dimohon mendatangkan hujan dalam ritual. Pada jubah istana, naga merujuk pada mandat kaisar untuk memerintah dari Takhta Naga. Museum V&A menafsirkan mutiara menyala dalam motif naga sebagai kebijaksanaan, pencerahan, dan hakikat spiritual. Pola naga pada keramik ekspor Tiongkok mengilhami keramik cetak biru-putih Inggris abad kesembilan belas. V&A mencatat bahwa pola piring Inggris mengikuti porselen biru-putih yang diekspor dari Tiongkok pada abad ketujuh belas dan kedelapan belas.
long_description.en:
Loong belongs to Chinese mythology and commonly has a serpentine shape with four legs. The dragon served as an emblem of imperial authority in Chinese history.

Coiled dragon forms occur on jade amulets from the Shang period. Scientific examination identifies many objects called dragon bones as mammal fossils. Wang Fu recorded a tradition of nine animal resemblances in dragon anatomy. Doré records an anatomical variant with deer antlers and a crocodile head. Art often shows dragons pursuing or contesting a flaming pearl. Popular belief connects dragons with rivers, seas, and the distribution of rain. During drought or flooding, villagers offered sacrifices and religious rites to appease local dragon kings and seek rain. One legend describes the Yellow Emperor ascending to heaven after becoming a dragon. The Norton Museum describes dragons as heavenly rulers petitioned for rain through ritual. On court robes, dragon imagery refers to the emperor’s mandate to rule from the Dragon Throne. The V&A interprets the flaming pearl in dragon imagery as wisdom, enlightenment, and spiritual essence. Dragon patterns on Chinese export ceramics inspired British printed blue-and-white wares in the nineteenth century. The V&A notes that the British plate pattern follows blue-and-white porcelain exported from China in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries.

claims_provenance.quote: The Chinese dragon, known as long or loong (/lʊŋ/ LUUNG) is a legendary creature in Chinese mythology, Chinese folklore, and Chinese culture generally. Chinese dragons have many animal-like forms, such as turtles and fish, but are most commonly depicted as snake-like with four legs.

claim.id: Naga menjadi lambang kekuasaan kaisar dalam sejarah Tiongkok.
claim.en: The dragon served as an emblem of imperial authority in Chinese history.

claims_provenance.quote: Historically, the Chinese dragon was associated with the emperor of China and used as a symbol to represent imperial power. Liu Bang, the founder of the Han dynasty, claimed that he was conceived after his mother dreamt of a dragon. During the Tang dynasty, emperors wore robes with dragon motif as an imperial symbol, and high officials might also be presented with dragon robes.

claim.id: Bentuk naga melingkar juga ditemukan pada amulet giok zaman Shang.
claim.en: Coiled dragon forms occur on jade amulets from the Shang period.

claims_provenance.quote: The coiled dragon or snake form played an important role in early Chinese culture. The character for "dragon" in the earliest Chinese writing has a similar coiled form, as do later jade dragon amulets from the Shang period.

claim.id: Sebagian benda yang dahulu disebut tulang naga ternyata fosil mamalia.
claim.en: Scientific examination identifies many objects called dragon bones as mammal fossils.

claims_provenance.quote: Scientific examination of "dragon bones" from the 19th century to the present suggests they most commonly are remains of fossil Cenozoic mammals, such as the extinct horse Hipparion.

claim.id: Wang Fu mencatat tradisi sembilan kemiripan anatomi naga dengan hewan lain.
claim.en: Wang Fu recorded a tradition of nine animal resemblances in dragon anatomy.

claims_provenance.quote: From its origins as totems or the stylized depiction of natural creatures, the Chinese dragon evolved to become a mythical animal. The Han dynasty scholar Wang Fu recorded Chinese myths that long dragons had nine anatomical resemblances.

claim.id: Doré mencatat varian anatomi dengan tanduk rusa dan kepala buaya.
claim.en: Doré records an anatomical variant with deer antlers and a crocodile head.

claims_provenance.quote: "The antlers of a deer. The head of a crocodile. A demon's eyes. The neck of a snake. A tortoise's viscera. A hawk's claws. The palms of a tiger. A cow's ears. And it hears through its horns, its ears being deprived of all power of hearing".

claim.id: Naga dalam seni sering mengejar atau memperebutkan mutiara menyala.
claim.en: Art often shows dragons pursuing or contesting a flaming pearl.

claims_provenance.quote: Many pictures of Chinese dragons show a flaming pearl under their chin or in their claws. The pearl is associated with spiritual energy, wisdom, prosperity, power, immortality, thunder, or the moon. Chinese art often depicts a pair of dragons chasing or fighting over a flaming pearl.

claim.id: Kepercayaan populer menghubungkan naga dengan sungai, laut, dan pengaturan hujan.
claim.en: Popular belief connects dragons with rivers, seas, and the distribution of rain.

claims_provenance.quote: Chinese dragons are strongly associated with water and weather in popular religion. They are believed to be the rulers of moving bodies of water, such as waterfalls, rivers, or seas. The Dragon god is the dispenser of rain as well as the zoomorphic representation of yang, the masculine power of generation.

claim.id: Saat kekeringan atau banjir, masyarakat melakukan ritual untuk memohon bantuan raja naga setempat.
claim.en: During drought or flooding, villagers offered sacrifices and religious rites to appease local dragon kings and seek rain.

claims_provenance.quote: Because of this association, they are seen as "in charge" of water-related weather phenomena. In premodern times, many Chinese villages (especially those close to rivers and seas) had temples dedicated to their local "dragon king".

claim.id: Sebuah legenda mengisahkan Kaisar Kuning naik ke langit setelah menjadi naga.
claim.en: One legend describes the Yellow Emperor ascending to heaven after becoming a dragon.

claims_provenance.quote: According to Chinese legend, both Chinese primogenitors, the earliest Door and the Yellow Emperor, were closely related to the dragon. At the end of his reign, the first legendary ruler, the Yellow Emperor, was said to have been immortalized into a dragon that resembled his emblem, and ascended to Heaven.

claim.id: Museum Norton menjelaskan naga sebagai penguasa langit yang dimohon mendatangkan hujan dalam ritual.
claim.en: The Norton Museum describes dragons as heavenly rulers petitioned for rain through ritual.

claims_provenance.quote: Each work depicts dragons, the heavenly sovereigns, petitioned to bring rain in ritual ceremonies.
claims_provenance.source_citation: Norton Museum of Art — Dragons: Commanders of Rain | Norton Museum of Art

short_description.id: Loong adalah naga dalam mitologi Tiongkok, lazim digambarkan menyerupai ular dengan empat kaki.
short_description.en: Loong belongs to Chinese mythology and commonly has a serpentine shape with four legs.

long_description.id: Loong adalah naga dalam mitologi Tiongkok, lazim digambarkan menyerupai ular dengan empat kaki. Naga menjadi lambang kekuasaan kaisar dalam sejarah Tiongkok.
long_description.en: Loong belongs to Chinese mythology and commonly has a serpentine shape with four legs. The dragon served as an emblem of imperial authority in Chinese history.

long_description.id: Bentuk naga melingkar juga ditemukan pada amulet giok zaman Shang. Sebagian benda yang dahulu disebut tulang naga ternyata fosil mamalia. Wang Fu mencatat tradisi sembilan kemiripan anatomi naga dengan hewan lain. Doré mencatat varian anatomi dengan tanduk rusa dan kepala buaya. Naga dalam seni sering mengejar atau memperebutkan mutiara menyala. Kepercayaan populer menghubungkan naga dengan sungai, laut, dan pengaturan hujan. Saat kekeringan atau banjir, masyarakat melakukan ritual untuk memohon bantuan raja naga setempat. Sebuah legenda mengisahkan Kaisar Kuning naik ke langit setelah menjadi naga. Museum Norton menjelaskan naga sebagai penguasa langit yang dimohon mendatangkan hujan dalam ritual. Pada jubah istana, naga merujuk pada mandat kaisar untuk memerintah dari Takhta Naga. Museum V&A menafsirkan mutiara menyala dalam motif naga sebagai kebijaksanaan, pencerahan, dan hakikat spiritual. Pola naga pada keramik ekspor Tiongkok mengilhami keramik cetak biru-putih Inggris abad kesembilan belas. V&A mencatat bahwa pola piring Inggris mengikuti porselen biru-putih yang diekspor dari Tiongkok pada abad ketujuh belas dan kedelapan belas.
long_description.en: Coiled dragon forms occur on jade amulets from the Shang period. Scientific examination identifies many objects called dragon bones as mammal fossils. Wang Fu recorded a tradition of nine animal resemblances in dragon anatomy. Doré records an anatomical variant with deer antlers and a crocodile head. Art often shows dragons pursuing or contesting a flaming pearl. Popular belief connects dragons with rivers, seas, and the distribution of rain. During drought or flooding, villagers offered sacrifices and religious rites to appease local dragon kings and seek rain. One legend describes the Yellow Emperor ascending to heaven after becoming a dragon. The Norton Museum describes dragons as heavenly rulers petitioned for rain through ritual. On court robes, dragon imagery refers to the emperor’s mandate to rule from the Dragon Throne. The V&A interprets the flaming pearl in dragon imagery as wisdom, enlightenment, and spiritual essence. Dragon patterns on Chinese export ceramics inspired British printed blue-and-white wares in the nineteenth century. The V&A notes that the British plate pattern follows blue-and-white porcelain exported from China in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries.

claims.quote: The Chinese dragon, known as long or loong (/lʊŋ/ LUUNG) is a legendary creature in Chinese mythology, Chinese folklore, and Chinese culture generally. Chinese dragons have many animal-like forms, such as turtles and fish, but are most commonly depicted as snake-like with four legs.

statement.id: Loong adalah naga dalam mitologi Tiongkok, lazim digambarkan menyerupai ular dengan empat kaki.
statement.en: Loong belongs to Chinese mythology and commonly has a serpentine shape with four legs.

claims.quote: Historically, the Chinese dragon was associated with the emperor of China and used as a symbol to represent imperial power. Liu Bang, the founder of the Han dynasty, claimed that he was conceived after his mother dreamt of a dragon. During the Tang dynasty, emperors wore robes with dragon motif as an imperial symbol, and high officials might also be presented with dragon robes.

statement.id: Naga menjadi lambang kekuasaan kaisar dalam sejarah Tiongkok.
statement.en: The dragon served as an emblem of imperial authority in Chinese history.

claims.quote: The coiled dragon or snake form played an important role in early Chinese culture. The character for "dragon" in the earliest Chinese writing has a similar coiled form, as do later jade dragon amulets from the Shang period.

statement.id: Bentuk naga melingkar juga ditemukan pada amulet giok zaman Shang.
statement.en: Coiled dragon forms occur on jade amulets from the Shang period.

claims.quote: Scientific examination of "dragon bones" from the 19th century to the present suggests they most commonly are remains of fossil Cenozoic mammals, such as the extinct horse Hipparion.

statement.id: Sebagian benda yang dahulu disebut tulang naga ternyata fosil mamalia.
statement.en: Scientific examination identifies many objects called dragon bones as mammal fossils.

claims.quote: From its origins as totems or the stylized depiction of natural creatures, the Chinese dragon evolved to become a mythical animal. The Han dynasty scholar Wang Fu recorded Chinese myths that long dragons had nine anatomical resemblances.

statement.id: Wang Fu mencatat tradisi sembilan kemiripan anatomi naga dengan hewan lain.
statement.en: Wang Fu recorded a tradition of nine animal resemblances in dragon anatomy.

claims.quote: "The antlers of a deer. The head of a crocodile. A demon's eyes. The neck of a snake. A tortoise's viscera. A hawk's claws. The palms of a tiger. A cow's ears. And it hears through its horns, its ears being deprived of all power of hearing".

statement.id: Doré mencatat varian anatomi dengan tanduk rusa dan kepala buaya.
statement.en: Doré records an anatomical variant with deer antlers and a crocodile head.

claims.quote: Many pictures of Chinese dragons show a flaming pearl under their chin or in their claws. The pearl is associated with spiritual energy, wisdom, prosperity, power, immortality, thunder, or the moon. Chinese art often depicts a pair of dragons chasing or fighting over a flaming pearl.

statement.id: Naga dalam seni sering mengejar atau memperebutkan mutiara menyala.
statement.en: Art often shows dragons pursuing or contesting a flaming pearl.

claims.quote: Chinese dragons are strongly associated with water and weather in popular religion. They are believed to be the rulers of moving bodies of water, such as waterfalls, rivers, or seas. The Dragon god is the dispenser of rain as well as the zoomorphic representation of yang, the masculine power of generation.

statement.id: Kepercayaan populer menghubungkan naga dengan sungai, laut, dan pengaturan hujan.
statement.en: Popular belief connects dragons with rivers, seas, and the distribution of rain.

claims.quote: Because of this association, they are seen as "in charge" of water-related weather phenomena. In premodern times, many Chinese villages (especially those close to rivers and seas) had temples dedicated to their local "dragon king".

statement.id: Saat kekeringan atau banjir, masyarakat melakukan ritual untuk memohon bantuan raja naga setempat.
statement.en: During drought or flooding, villagers offered sacrifices and religious rites to appease local dragon kings and seek rain.

claims.quote: According to Chinese legend, both Chinese primogenitors, the earliest Door and the Yellow Emperor, were closely related to the dragon. At the end of his reign, the first legendary ruler, the Yellow Emperor, was said to have been immortalized into a dragon that resembled his emblem, and ascended to Heaven.

statement.id: Sebuah legenda mengisahkan Kaisar Kuning naik ke langit setelah menjadi naga.
statement.en: One legend describes the Yellow Emperor ascending to heaven after becoming a dragon.

claims.quote: Each work depicts dragons, the heavenly sovereigns, petitioned to bring rain in ritual ceremonies.

short_description.id: Markut, juga disebut Merküt atau Bürküt, adalah burung legendaris berwujud elang dalam tradisi Altai dan Mongol yang melindungi dan membimbing dukun; di kalangan Yörük di Anatolia ia menjadi sosok untuk menakuti anak nakal.
short_description.en: Markut, also called Merküt or Bürküt, is a legendary eagle-like bird of Altay and Mongol tradition that protects and guides shamans; among the Yörüks of Anatolia it became a figure used to frighten naughty children.

long_description.id:
Menurut kamus kedua, Markut adalah elang legendaris dalam mitologi Altai dan Mongol. Ia menjaga para dukun, menuntun jiwa mereka saat melakukan perjalanan ke langit, dan menggendong mereka kembali ke bumi bila tenaga mereka habis. Dalam doa dukun Altai, ia disapa sebagai burung yang sayap kirinya menutupi Bulan, sayap kanannya Matahari, dan sebagai ibu sembilan elang.

Artikel pertama mengutip catatan Radlov tentang ritual kurban dukun di Pegunungan Altai. Markut di sana tidak kasatmata, hanya bisa dilihat orang tertentu, dan dipanggil untuk mengusir roh jahat. Setelah burung itu menjawab panggilan, dukun menirukan suaranya lalu menekuk leher untuk memperlihatkan beratnya memikul burung besar itu.

Pada genderang dukun Teleüt terdapat gambar burung berwujud elang besar bernama Ülgen kuşu Bay Mörküt, dan dalam pandangan dukun Altay-Sayan burung berwajah cahaya yang menemani Ülgen saat ritual juga disebut Merküt. Artikel pertama juga melihat kedekatan makna antara Markut, Bürküt Ata pada orang Turkmen, dan kepercayaan Yakut bahwa dukun berasal dari keturunan Bürküt.

Jauh dari Siberia, di kalangan Yörük semi-nomaden di Anatolia, Merküt menjadi makhluk khayalan yang dikaitkan dengan anak-anak. Di sana ia dikenal sebagai burung legendaris yang dipakai untuk menakut-nakuti anak nakal, dan menurut kepercayaan lama ia hanya menakuti orang yang namanya disebut.
long_description.en:
According to the second source, Markut is a legendary eagle in Altay and Mongol mythology. It watches over shamans, leads their souls on the journey into the sky and carries them back down to earth on its back once their strength fails. Altai shamans' prayers address it as the bird whose left wing hides the Moon and whose right wing hides the Sun, and as the mother of nine eagles.

The first article draws on Radlov's account of shamans' sacrificial rites in the Altay mountains. There Markut is unseen, visible only to certain people, and is called upon to scare off evil spirits. Once the bird answers the call, the shaman imitates its cry and then bends his neck to show how heavy the great bird is to bear.

Teleüt shamans' drums bear the image of a great eagle-like bird called Ülgen kuşu Bay Mörküt, and in the Altay-Sayan shamans' view the light-faced bird that accompanies Ülgen during rites is likewise called Merküt. The first article also notes a closeness in meaning between Markut, Bürküt Ata of the Turkmens and the Yakut belief that shamans descend from the Bürküt line.

Far from Siberia, among the semi-nomadic Yörüks of Anatolia, Merküt became an imaginary being connected with children. There it is known as a legendary bird used to scare naughty children, and in the old belief it frightens only those whose names are spoken.

claim.id: Markut, Merküt, atau Bürküt adalah burung legendaris (efsanevi kuş) di kalangan Yörük (Yörükler) yang direka untuk menakuti anak nakal; menurut kepercayaan lama, ia hanya menakuti orang yang namanya disebut.
claim.en: Markut, Merküt or Bürküt is a legendary bird (efsanevi kuş) among the Yörüks (Yörükler), invented to frighten naughty children; according to the old belief it only frightens those whose names are mentioned.

claims_provenance.quote: Markut, Merküt veya Bürküt, Yörükler arasında yaramazlık yapan çocukları korkutmak için uydurulan efsanevi kuş. Eski inanışa göre, Markut sadece adı anılanları korkutan bir kuştur.

claim.id: Burung Markut yang dipanggil untuk menakuti roh jahat (kötü ruhları) memiliki kedekatan makna mitologis dengan Bürküt Ata pada orang Turkmen (Türkmenlerdeki) dan dengan kepercayaan Yakut (Yakutların) bahwa para dukun (şamanların) berasal dari keturunan Bürküt.
claim.en: The bird Markut, summoned to frighten evil spirits (kötü ruhları), is mythologically close to Bürküt Ata among the Turkmens (Türkmenlerdeki) and to the Yakut (Yakutların) belief that shamans (şamanların) descend from the Bürküt lineage.

claims_provenance.quote: Kötü ruhları korkutmak amacıyla çağırılan Markut adındaki bu kuş ile Türkmenlerdeki Bürküt Ata ve Yakutların, şamanların Bürküt soyundan gelme inançları arasında mitolojik anlamsallık açısından yakınlık bulunmaktadır.

claim.id: Markut yang disebut Radlov tidak terlihat mata (göze görünmez) dan dipanggil untuk menakuti roh jahat; hanya orang tertentu (belli insanlar) yang dapat melihatnya.
claim.en: The Markut mentioned by Radlov is invisible (göze görünmez) and is summoned to frighten evil spirits; only certain people (belli insanlar) can see it.

claims_provenance.quote: Radlov'un sözünü ettiği Markut, göze görünmez ve kötü ruhları korkutmak için çağırılır. Bu kuşu ancak belli insanlar tarafından görüşebilir.

claim.id: Setelah dukun (şaman) memanggil burung Markut dengan cara ini dan burung itu menjawab, ia menirukan suara burung (kuşun sesini taklit eder).
claim.en: After the shaman (şaman) summons the Markut bird in this way and it answers, he imitates the bird's voice (kuşun sesini taklit eder).

claims_provenance.quote: Şaman, Markut kuşunu bu yolla çağırdıktan sonra cevap verdiği zaman, kuşun sesini taklit eder

claim.id: Lalu ia menekuk lehernya (boynunu büker) untuk menunjukkan betapa beratnya membawa burung besar itu (büyük kuşun).
claim.en: Then he bends his neck (boynunu büker) to show how hard it is to carry the great bird (büyük kuşun).

claims_provenance.quote: Sonra büyük kuşun taşımasının ne kadar zor olduğunu göstermek için boynunu büker.

claim.id: Salah satu gambar pada genderang dukun Teleüt (Teleüt şamanlarının davullarında) adalah burung bernama Ülgen kuşu Bay Mörküt yang berwujud elang besar.
claim.en: One of the images on the drums of Teleüt shamans (Teleüt şamanlarının davullarında) is a bird called Ülgen kuşu Bay Mörküt, shaped like a great eagle.

claims_provenance.quote: Teleüt şamanlarının davullarında yer alan resimlerden biri de "Ülgen kuşu Bay Mörküt" adında büyük kartal görünüşlü bir kuştur.

claim.id: Dalam pandangan dunia dukun Altay-Sayan, burung berwajah cahaya (nur yüzlü kuş) yang menemani Ülgen saat ritual dukun (kamlık) juga bernama Merküt.
claim.en: In the worldview of the Altay-Sayan shamans, the light-faced bird (nur yüzlü kuş) accompanying Ülgen during the shamanic rite (kamlık) is also named Merküt.

claims_provenance.quote: Böylece Altay-Sayan şamanlarının dünya görüşünde kamlık zamanı ulu Ülgen'e yoldaşlık yapan nur yüzlü kuşun adı da "Merküt" olmuştur.

claim.id: Burung Merküt ini, jauh dari Siberia (Sibirya), dalam tradisi Yörük semi-nomaden Anatolia (Anadolu) berubah menjadi makhluk khayalan yang melindungi anak-anak (çocukları koruyan).
claim.en: This Merküt bird, far from Siberia (Sibirya), took the form among the semi-nomadic Yörüks of Anatolia (Anadolu) of an imaginary being that protects children (çocukları koruyan).

claims_provenance.quote: kuşu, Sibirya'dan çok uzaklarda, aynı etnik-kültürel sistemin binlerce kilometre uzağında yaşayan başka bir geleneğinde Anadolu'nun yarı göçebe Yörüklerinin dilinde çocukları koruyan hayali bir varlık şeklini almıştır.

claim.id: Markut adalah elang legendaris (efsânevî kartal) dalam mitologi Altai (Altay) dan Mongol (Moğol); ia melindungi para dukun (şamanları korur) dan membimbing jiwa mereka dalam perjalanan ke langit (göğe yaptıkları yolculukta).
claim.en: Markut is the legendary eagle (efsânevî kartal) of Altay and Mongol (Moğol) mythology; it protects shamans (şamanları korur) and guides their souls on their journey to the sky (göğe yaptıkları yolculukta).

claims_provenance.quote: Altay ve Moğol mitolojisindeki efsânevî kartaldır. Şamanları korur ve göğe yaptıkları yolculukta yardımcı olarak ruhlarına kılavuzluk eder.

claim.en: When their strength runs out (güçleri tükenince), it carries them down to earth on its back; the motif is also found among the Yörük tribes of Anatolia (Anadolu'da yörük boyları).

claims_provenance.quote: Güçleri tükenince sırtında yeryüzüne indirir. Anadolu'da yörük boyları arasında da rastlanan bir motiftir.

claim.en: In Altai shamans' prayers the bird is addressed: its left wing covers the Moon (Ay), its right wing the Sun (Güneş), O mother of nine eagles (dokuz kartalın anası).

short_description.id: Markut, juga disebut Merküt atau Bürküt, adalah burung legendaris berwujud elang dalam tradisi Altai dan Mongol yang melindungi dan membimbing dukun; di kalangan Yörük di Anatolia ia menjadi sosok untuk menakuti anak nakal.
short_description.en: Markut, also called Merküt or Bürküt, is a legendary eagle-like bird of Altay and Mongol tradition that protects and guides shamans; among the Yörüks of Anatolia it became a figure used to frighten naughty children.

long_description.id: Menurut kamus kedua, Markut adalah elang legendaris dalam mitologi Altai dan Mongol. Ia menjaga para dukun, menuntun jiwa mereka saat melakukan perjalanan ke langit, dan menggendong mereka kembali ke bumi bila tenaga mereka habis. Dalam doa dukun Altai, ia disapa sebagai burung yang sayap kirinya menutupi Bulan, sayap kanannya Matahari, dan sebagai ibu sembilan elang.
long_description.en: According to the second source, Markut is a legendary eagle in Altay and Mongol mythology. It watches over shamans, leads their souls on the journey into the sky and carries them back down to earth on its back once their strength fails. Altai shamans' prayers address it as the bird whose left wing hides the Moon and whose right wing hides the Sun, and as the mother of nine eagles.

long_description.id: Artikel pertama mengutip catatan Radlov tentang ritual kurban dukun di Pegunungan Altai. Markut di sana tidak kasatmata, hanya bisa dilihat orang tertentu, dan dipanggil untuk mengusir roh jahat. Setelah burung itu menjawab panggilan, dukun menirukan suaranya lalu menekuk leher untuk memperlihatkan beratnya memikul burung besar itu.
long_description.en: The first article draws on Radlov's account of shamans' sacrificial rites in the Altay mountains. There Markut is unseen, visible only to certain people, and is called upon to scare off evil spirits. Once the bird answers the call, the shaman imitates its cry and then bends his neck to show how heavy the great bird is to bear.

long_description.id: Pada genderang dukun Teleüt terdapat gambar burung berwujud elang besar bernama Ülgen kuşu Bay Mörküt, dan dalam pandangan dukun Altay-Sayan burung berwajah cahaya yang menemani Ülgen saat ritual juga disebut Merküt. Artikel pertama juga melihat kedekatan makna antara Markut, Bürküt Ata pada orang Turkmen, dan kepercayaan Yakut bahwa dukun berasal dari keturunan Bürküt.
long_description.en: Teleüt shamans' drums bear the image of a great eagle-like bird called Ülgen kuşu Bay Mörküt, and in the Altay-Sayan shamans' view the light-faced bird that accompanies Ülgen during rites is likewise called Merküt. The first article also notes a closeness in meaning between Markut, Bürküt Ata of the Turkmens and the Yakut belief that shamans descend from the Bürküt line.

long_description.id: Jauh dari Siberia, di kalangan Yörük semi-nomaden di Anatolia, Merküt menjadi makhluk khayalan yang dikaitkan dengan anak-anak. Di sana ia dikenal sebagai burung legendaris yang dipakai untuk menakut-nakuti anak nakal, dan menurut kepercayaan lama ia hanya menakuti orang yang namanya disebut.
long_description.en: Far from Siberia, among the semi-nomadic Yörüks of Anatolia, Merküt became an imaginary being connected with children. There it is known as a legendary bird used to scare naughty children, and in the old belief it frightens only those whose names are spoken.

claims.quote: Markut, Merküt veya Bürküt, Yörükler arasında yaramazlık yapan çocukları korkutmak için uydurulan efsanevi kuş. Eski inanışa göre, Markut sadece adı anılanları korkutan bir kuştur.

statement.id: Markut, Merküt, atau Bürküt adalah burung legendaris (efsanevi kuş) di kalangan Yörük (Yörükler) yang direka untuk menakuti anak nakal; menurut kepercayaan lama, ia hanya menakuti orang yang namanya disebut.
statement.en: Markut, Merküt or Bürküt is a legendary bird (efsanevi kuş) among the Yörüks (Yörükler), invented to frighten naughty children; according to the old belief it only frightens those whose names are mentioned.

claims.quote: Kötü ruhları korkutmak amacıyla çağırılan Markut adındaki bu kuş ile Türkmenlerdeki Bürküt Ata ve Yakutların, şamanların Bürküt soyundan gelme inançları arasında mitolojik anlamsallık açısından yakınlık bulunmaktadır.

statement.id: Burung Markut yang dipanggil untuk menakuti roh jahat (kötü ruhları) memiliki kedekatan makna mitologis dengan Bürküt Ata pada orang Turkmen (Türkmenlerdeki) dan dengan kepercayaan Yakut (Yakutların) bahwa para dukun (şamanların) berasal dari keturunan Bürküt.
statement.en: The bird Markut, summoned to frighten evil spirits (kötü ruhları), is mythologically close to Bürküt Ata among the Turkmens (Türkmenlerdeki) and to the Yakut (Yakutların) belief that shamans (şamanların) descend from the Bürküt lineage.

claims.quote: Radlov'un sözünü ettiği Markut, göze görünmez ve kötü ruhları korkutmak için çağırılır. Bu kuşu ancak belli insanlar tarafından görüşebilir.

statement.id: Markut yang disebut Radlov tidak terlihat mata (göze görünmez) dan dipanggil untuk menakuti roh jahat; hanya orang tertentu (belli insanlar) yang dapat melihatnya.
statement.en: The Markut mentioned by Radlov is invisible (göze görünmez) and is summoned to frighten evil spirits; only certain people (belli insanlar) can see it.

claims.quote: Şaman, Markut kuşunu bu yolla çağırdıktan sonra cevap verdiği zaman, kuşun sesini taklit eder

statement.id: Setelah dukun (şaman) memanggil burung Markut dengan cara ini dan burung itu menjawab, ia menirukan suara burung (kuşun sesini taklit eder).
statement.en: After the shaman (şaman) summons the Markut bird in this way and it answers, he imitates the bird's voice (kuşun sesini taklit eder).

claims.quote: Sonra büyük kuşun taşımasının ne kadar zor olduğunu göstermek için boynunu büker.

statement.id: Lalu ia menekuk lehernya (boynunu büker) untuk menunjukkan betapa beratnya membawa burung besar itu (büyük kuşun).
statement.en: Then he bends his neck (boynunu büker) to show how hard it is to carry the great bird (büyük kuşun).

claims.quote: Teleüt şamanlarının davullarında yer alan resimlerden biri de "Ülgen kuşu Bay Mörküt" adında büyük kartal görünüşlü bir kuştur.

statement.id: Salah satu gambar pada genderang dukun Teleüt (Teleüt şamanlarının davullarında) adalah burung bernama Ülgen kuşu Bay Mörküt yang berwujud elang besar.
statement.en: One of the images on the drums of Teleüt shamans (Teleüt şamanlarının davullarında) is a bird called Ülgen kuşu Bay Mörküt, shaped like a great eagle.

claims.quote: Böylece Altay-Sayan şamanlarının dünya görüşünde kamlık zamanı ulu Ülgen'e yoldaşlık yapan nur yüzlü kuşun adı da "Merküt" olmuştur.

statement.id: Dalam pandangan dunia dukun Altay-Sayan, burung berwajah cahaya (nur yüzlü kuş) yang menemani Ülgen saat ritual dukun (kamlık) juga bernama Merküt.
statement.en: In the worldview of the Altay-Sayan shamans, the light-faced bird (nur yüzlü kuş) accompanying Ülgen during the shamanic rite (kamlık) is also named Merküt.

claims.quote: kuşu, Sibirya'dan çok uzaklarda, aynı etnik-kültürel sistemin binlerce kilometre uzağında yaşayan başka bir geleneğinde Anadolu'nun yarı göçebe Yörüklerinin dilinde çocukları koruyan hayali bir varlık şeklini almıştır.

statement.id: Burung Merküt ini, jauh dari Siberia (Sibirya), dalam tradisi Yörük semi-nomaden Anatolia (Anadolu) berubah menjadi makhluk khayalan yang melindungi anak-anak (çocukları koruyan).
statement.en: This Merküt bird, far from Siberia (Sibirya), took the form among the semi-nomadic Yörüks of Anatolia (Anadolu) of an imaginary being that protects children (çocukları koruyan).

claims.quote: Altay ve Moğol mitolojisindeki efsânevî kartaldır. Şamanları korur ve göğe yaptıkları yolculukta yardımcı olarak ruhlarına kılavuzluk eder.

statement.id: Markut adalah elang legendaris (efsânevî kartal) dalam mitologi Altai (Altay) dan Mongol (Moğol); ia melindungi para dukun (şamanları korur) dan membimbing jiwa mereka dalam perjalanan ke langit (göğe yaptıkları yolculukta).
statement.en: Markut is the legendary eagle (efsânevî kartal) of Altay and Mongol (Moğol) mythology; it protects shamans (şamanları korur) and guides their souls on their journey to the sky (göğe yaptıkları yolculukta).

claims.quote: Güçleri tükenince sırtında yeryüzüne indirir. Anadolu'da yörük boyları arasında da rastlanan bir motiftir.

statement.id: Ketika tenaga mereka habis (güçleri tükenince), ia membawa mereka turun ke bumi di punggungnya; motif ini juga dijumpai di antara suku Yörük di Anatolia (Anadolu'da yörük boyları).
statement.en: When their strength runs out (güçleri tükenince), it carries them down to earth on its back; the motif is also found among the Yörük tribes of Anatolia (Anadolu'da yörük boyları).

claims.quote: Sol kanadı Ay'ı örter/Sağ kanadı Güneş'i/Ey dokuz kartalın anası!

statement.id: Dalam doa dukun Altai, burung ini disapa: sayap kirinya menutupi Bulan (Ay), sayap kanannya Matahari (Güneş), wahai ibu sembilan elang (dokuz kartalın anası).
statement.en: In Altai shamans' prayers the bird is addressed: its left wing covers the Moon (Ay), its right wing the Sun (Güneş), O mother of nine eagles (dokuz kartalın anası).

summary.id: Dalam tradisi dukun Altai dan Mongol, Markut adalah elang pelindung dan pembimbing dukun.
summary.en: In Altay and Mongol shamanic tradition, Markut is an eagle that protects and guides shamans.

summary.id: Di kalangan Yörük, Markut adalah burung yang direka untuk menakuti anak nakal, meski artikel pertama juga menyebutnya makhluk yang melindungi anak.
summary.en: Among the Yörüks, Markut is a bird invented to frighten naughty children, though the first article also calls it a being that protects children.

short_description.id: Elang tanpa nama di puncak Yggdrasil adalah burung dalam mitologi Nordik yang bertengger di puncak pohon dunia, dengan elang kecil Veðrfölnir di antara kedua matanya, dan berselisih dengan naga Nidhöggr di akar pohon.
short_description.en: The unnamed eagle on the top of Yggdrasil is a bird of Norse mythology perched atop the world tree, with the hawk Veðrfölnir between its eyes, and at odds with the dragon Nidhöggr at the tree's roots.

long_description.id:
Dalam mitologi Nordik, seekor elang yang namanya tidak diketahui bertengger di puncak pohon dunia Yggdrasil, dan di antara kedua matanya duduk elang kecil Veðrfölnir. Elang ini tercatat dalam Edda Puitis, yang dihimpun pada abad ke-13 dari bahan tradisional yang lebih tua, dan dalam Edda Prosa karya Snorri Sturluson, sedangkan Veðrfölnir hanya disebut dalam Edda Prosa.

Dalam Grímnismál, tupai Ratatoskr berlari di pohon ash Yggdrasil membawa kata-kata elang itu dari atas dan menyampaikannya kepada Nidhöggr di bawah. Dalam Gylfaginning dijelaskan bahwa seekor elang duduk di puncak pohon ash dan "mengetahui banyak hal", sementara Ratatoskr membawa gunjingan fitnah yang memancing permusuhan elang dan Nidhöggr. Bait Völuspá tentang "elang yang memekik" pada awal Ragnarök mungkin juga merujuk elang ini.

John Lindow mencatat bahwa Snorri tidak menjelaskan mengapa elang kecil duduk di antara mata elang atau apa perannya; menurutnya elang kecil itu barangkali terkait dengan kebijaksanaan elang, dan mungkin, seperti burung gagak Odin, terbang mengumpulkan dan membawa pulang pengetahuan.
long_description.en:
In Norse mythology an eagle whose name is unknown perches at the top of the world tree Yggdrasil, and between its eyes sits the hawk Veðrfölnir. The eagle is attested in the Poetic Edda, compiled in the 13th century from older traditional material, and in Snorri Sturluson's Prose Edda, whereas Veðrfölnir appears only in the Prose Edda.

In Grímnismál the squirrel Ratatoskr runs on the ash Yggdrasil carrying the eagle's words from above and telling them to Nidhöggr below. Gylfaginning explains that an eagle sits at the top of the ash and 'has knowledge of many things', while Ratatoskr carries slanderous gossip that stirs up the eagle and Nidhöggr. The Völuspá verse about a 'screeching eagle' at the onset of Ragnarök may also refer to this eagle.

John Lindow notes that Snorri does not say why a hawk should sit between the eagle's eyes or what role it plays; he suggests the hawk is presumably tied to the eagle's wisdom and perhaps, like Odin's ravens, flies off to gather and bring back knowledge.

long_description.en: In Grímnismál the squirrel Ratatoskr runs on the ash Yggdrasil carrying the eagle's words from above and telling them to Nidhöggr below. Gylfaginning explains that an eagle sits at the top of the ash and 'has knowledge of many things', while Ratatoskr carries slanderous gossip that stirs up the eagle and Nidhöggr. The Völuspá verse about a 'screeching eagle' at the onset of Ragnarök may also refer to this eagle.

long_description.id: John Lindow mencatat bahwa Snorri tidak menjelaskan mengapa elang kecil duduk di antara mata elang atau apa perannya; menurutnya elang kecil itu barangkali terkait dengan kebijaksanaan elang, dan mungkin, seperti burung gagak Odin, terbang mengumpulkan dan membawa pulang pengetahuan.
long_description.en: John Lindow notes that Snorri does not say why a hawk should sit between the eagle's eyes or what role it plays; he suggests the hawk is presumably tied to the eagle's wisdom and perhaps, like Odin's ravens, flies off to gather and bring back knowledge.

claims.quote: In Norse mythology, Veðrfölnir (Old Norse "storm pale", "wind bleached", or "wind-witherer") is a hawk sitting between the eyes of an unnamed eagle that is perched on top of the world tree Yggdrasil.

statement.id: Dalam mitologi Nordik (Norse), Veðrfölnir adalah elang kecil yang duduk di antara kedua mata seekor elang tanpa nama yang bertengger di puncak pohon dunia Yggdrasil.
statement.en: In Norse mythology Veðrfölnir is a hawk sitting between the eyes of an unnamed eagle perched on top of the world tree Yggdrasil.

claims.quote: The unnamed eagle is attested in both the Poetic Edda, compiled in the 13th century from earlier traditional sources, and the Prose Edda, written in the 13th century by Snorri Sturluson, while Veðrfölnir is solely attested in the Prose Edda.

statement.id: Elang tanpa nama itu tercatat dalam Edda Puitis (Poetic Edda), dihimpun abad ke-13 dari sumber tradisional lebih tua, dan Edda Prosa (Prose Edda) karya Snorri Sturluson abad ke-13, sedangkan Veðrfölnir hanya di Edda Prosa.
statement.en: The unnamed eagle is attested in the Poetic Edda, compiled in the 13th century from older sources, and in Snorri Sturluson's 13th-century Prose Edda, while Veðrfölnir is only in the Prose Edda.

claims.quote: In both the Poetic Edda and the Prose Edda, the squirrel Ratatoskr carries messages between the unnamed eagle and Nidhöggr, the worm that resides below the world tree.

statement.id: Dalam kedua Edda, tupai Ratatoskr membawa pesan antara elang tanpa nama dan Nidhöggr, cacing atau naga yang tinggal di bawah pohon dunia.
statement.en: In both Eddas the squirrel Ratatoskr carries messages between the unnamed eagle and Nidhöggr, the worm dwelling below the world tree.

claims.quote: There is much to be told. An eagle sits at the top of the ash, and it has knowledge of many things. Between its eyes sits the hawk called Vedrfolnir [...]. The squirrel called Ratatosk runs up and down the ash. He tells slanderous gossip, provoking the eagle and Nidhogg.

statement.id: Gylfaginning: seekor elang duduk di puncak pohon ash dan mengetahui banyak hal; di antara matanya duduk elang kecil Vedrfolnir; tupai Ratatosk berlari naik-turun membawa gunjingan fitnah yang memancing elang dan Nidhogg.
statement.en: Gylfaginning: an eagle sits at the top of the ash with knowledge of many things; between its eyes sits the hawk Vedrfolnir; the squirrel Ratatosk runs up and down telling slanderous gossip that provokes the eagle and Nidhogg.

claims.quote: In der nordischen Mythologie gibt es einen Adler am Weltenbaum Yggdrasil, dessen Name unbekannt ist.

statement.id: Dalam mitologi Nordik (nordischen) ada seekor elang di pohon dunia Yggdrasil yang namanya tidak diketahui.
statement.en: In Norse (nordischen) mythology there is an eagle on the world tree Yggdrasil whose name is unknown.

claims.quote: Das Gegensatzpaar Adler–Nidhöggr deutet darauf hin, dass auch diese Stelle des Lieds Völuspá den Weltenbaum-Adler meint, da man davon ausgeht, dass mit dem Nasenbleichen wohl Nidhöggr gemeint ist. Die Textstelle handelt vom Beginn der Ragnarök, der Endzeit der Götter.

statement.id: Pasangan berlawanan elang–Nidhöggr menunjukkan bahwa bait Völuspá ini ("elang memekik") juga merujuk elang pohon dunia, karena "yang berhidung pucat" dianggap Nidhöggr; bait itu tentang awal Ragnarök.
statement.en: The eagle–Nidhöggr pairing suggests this Völuspá passage ('the eagle screams') also means the world-tree eagle, since the 'pale-nosed one' is taken to be Nidhöggr; the passage concerns the onset of Ragnarök.

claims.quote: John Lindow points out that Snorri does not say why a hawk should be sitting between the eyes of an eagle or what role it may play. Lindow theorizes that "presumably the hawk is associated with the wisdom of the eagle" and that "perhaps, like Odin's ravens, it flies off acquiring and bringing back knowledge".

statement.id: John Lindow menunjukkan bahwa Snorri tidak menjelaskan mengapa elang kecil duduk di antara mata elang atau apa perannya; Lindow menduga elang kecil itu terkait kebijaksanaan elang, dan mungkin, seperti gagak Odin, terbang mengumpulkan dan membawa pulang pengetahuan.
statement.en: John Lindow points out that Snorri does not say why a hawk sits between an eagle's eyes or what role it plays; Lindow suggests it is presumably linked to the eagle's wisdom and perhaps, like Odin's ravens, flies off gathering and bringing back knowledge.

claims.quote: From above the words of the eagle he bears, And tells them to Nithhogg beneath.

statement.id: Dalam Grímnismál (terjemahan Bellows), Ratatosk membawa kata-kata elang (words of the eagle) dari atas dan menyampaikannya kepada Nithhogg di bawah (beneath).
statement.en: In Grímnismál (Bellows's translation), Ratatosk bears the words of the eagle from above and tells them to Nithhogg beneath.

short_description.id: Akbuzat adalah kuda putih bersayap mitologi Turkik, leluhur totem bangsa Bashkir dan Tatar dan kuda pahlawan Ural-Batyr, yang tinggal di langit dan ditambatkan pada Bintang Utara.
short_description.en: Akbuzat is the white winged horse of Turkic mythology, totem ancestor of the Bashkir and Tatar peoples and Ural-Batyr's heroic steed, who lives in the sky tethered to the Pole Star.

long_description.id:
Akbuzat, "kuda bersayap yang terang", adalah kuda pahlawan dan leluhur totem bangsa-bangsa Turkik, lahir dari totemisme dan pemujaan kuda; warna putihnya melambangkan kehidupan dan kematian yang baik. Dalam mitologi Tatar, Akbuzat dan Kukbuzat tinggal di langit, turun membantu para pahlawan, lalu ditambatkan pada Bintang Utara sementara tujuh pencuri kuda, rasi Biduk, mengejar mereka tanpa hasil.

Dalam mitologi Bashkir ia leluhur para tulpar dan kuda Ural-Batyr dalam epos Akbuzat; ia tidak terbakar atau tenggelam, menghancurkan gunung dengan kukunya, dan busa mulutnya menyembuhkan luka. Opera Akbuzat dipentaskan pada 1942, dan monumennya berdiri di Burzyansky sejak 2021.
long_description.en:
Akbuzat, 'light winged horse', is a heroic horse and totem ancestor of the Turkic peoples, born of totemism and the horse cult; its whiteness stands for a good life and death. In Tatar mythology Akbuzat and Kukbuzat live in the sky, come down to help heroes and are tethered to the Pole Star, while seven horse thieves, the Great Bear, chase them in vain.

In Bashkir mythology it is ancestor of the tulpars and Ural-Batyr's horse in the epic Akbuzat; it neither burns nor drowns, smashes mountains with its hooves, and its mouth foam heals wounds. The opera Akbuzat was staged in 1942, and its monument has stood in Burzyansky since 2021.

claim.id: Akbuzat (Bashkir: Aҡbuҙat; Tatar: Akbuzat, "kuda bersayap yang terang") adalah tokoh cerita rakyat dan mitologi Turkik, leluhur totem bangsa-bangsa itu dan kuda pahlawan yang luhur.
claim.en: Akbuzat (Bashkir Aҡbuҙat; Tatar Akbuzat, 'light winged horse') is a figure of Turkic folklore and mythology, the totem ancestor of those peoples and a virtuous heroic horse.

claims_provenance.quote: Akbuthat (bachkir : Aҡbuҙat ; tatar : Akbuzat  - cheval ailé léger) est un personnage du folklore et de la mythologie turque, l'ancêtre (ancêtre totem) de ces peuples, et vertu héroïque du cheval.

claim.id: Asal-usul Akbuzat terkait luasnya totemisme di kalangan bangsa Turkik dan pemujaan kuda, sedangkan warna putih melambangkan kelahiran yang selamat, hidup bahagia, kematian damai, dan pemakaman yang layak.
claim.en: Akbuzat's origin is tied to widespread totemism among Turkic peoples and the cult of the horse, while white symbolises a safe birth, a happy life, a peaceful death and a worthy burial.

claims_provenance.quote: L'origine d'Akbuzat est liée à la large diffusion du totémisme parmi les peuples turciques, ainsi qu'au culte du cheval, qui jouait un rôle important dans la vie des Turcs. La couleur blanche symbolise une naissance réussie et heureuse, une vie, une mort paisible et un enterrement digne.

claim.id: Mitologi Tatar mengisahkan dua kuda pahlawan ilahi, Akbuzat dan Kukbuzat (kuda biru langit), yang hidup di langit, turun ke bumi membantu para pahlawan, lalu kembali ke langit dan ditambatkan pada tiang besi.
claim.en: Tatar mythology tells of two divine heroic horses, Akbuzat and Kukbuzat (the sky-blue horse), who live in the sky, come down to help heroes, then return to the sky, tied to an iron stake.

claims_provenance.quote: La mythologie tatare comprend l'histoire de deux chevaux héroïques divins, Akbuzat et Kukbuzat (cheval bleu ciel), vivant dans le ciel ; ces chevaux participent aux actions des héros, descendant sur terre, puis remontant au ciel, où ils sont attachés à un pieu de fer

claim.id: Menurut artikel bahasa Rusia, tiang besi itu adalah Timerkazyk (Bintang Utara) tempat mereka merumput, dan tujuh pencuri kuda (Biduk) terus mengejar Akbuzat dan Kukbuzat tetapi tak pernah dapat menyusul.
claim.en: According to the Russian article, the iron stake is Timerkazyk (the Pole Star) around which they graze, and seven horse thieves (the Great Bear) chase Akbuzat and Kukbuzat but can never catch them.

claims_provenance.quote: где они привязаны к железному колу (тат. Тимерказык — Полярная звезда) и пасутся вокруг него. Семь конокрадов (Большая Медведица) преследуют Акбузата и Кукбузата, с целью похищения, но догнать не могут.

claim.id: Dalam mitologi Bashkir ia kuda pahlawan bersayap yang ajaib, leluhur para tulpar, kuda Ural-Batyr, dan tokoh utama epos Bashkir (kubair) Akbuzat.
claim.en: In Bashkir mythology it is a magic winged heroic horse, ancestor of the tulpars, Ural-Batyr's horse and the title character of the Bashkir epic (kubair) Akbuzat.

claims_provenance.quote: Dans la mythologie bachkire, c'est un cheval héroïque ailé magique, ancêtre des Tulpars. Cheval d'Oural-Batyr, personnage principal de l'épopée bachkire (kubair) « Akbuzat ».

claim.id: Menurut artikel bahasa Bashkir, ia lahir di langit, dapat hidup di darat dan di bawah air, tidak terbakar api, tidak tenggelam, menghancurkan gunung dengan kukunya, dan membelah laut.
claim.en: According to the Bashkir article, it was born in the sky, can live on land and under water, does not burn in fire or sink in water, smashes mountains with its hooves and parts the sea.

claims_provenance.quote: Күктә тыуған, ерҙә һәм һыу аҫтында йәшәй ала, утта янмай, һыуҙа батмай, тояҡтары менән тауҙарҙы емерә һәм диңгеҙҙе айыра.

claim.id: Busa mulut Akbuzat berkhasiat menyembuhkan luka bila dioleskan.
claim.en: Akbuzat's mouth foam heals wounds when rubbed on them.

claims_provenance.quote: Аҡбуҙаттың ауыҙ күбеге шифалы — уны һөртөп, яраны бөтәштерәләр.

claim.id: Antonio Spadavecchia bersama Kh. Zaimov menulis opera Akbuzat ("Kuda Ajaib") yang pertama dipentaskan pada 1942 di Teater Opera dan Balet Negara Bashkir.
claim.en: Antonio Spadavecchia with Kh. Zaimov wrote the opera Akbuzat ('The Magic Horse'), first staged in 1942 at the Bashkir State Opera and Ballet Theatre.

claims_provenance.quote: Antonio Emmanuilovich Spadavecchia a écrit avec Kh. Zaimov l'opéra « Akbuzat » (« Le cheval magique »), créé pour la première fois en 1942 au Théâtre académique d'opéra et de ballet de l'État bachkir

claim.id: Pada 2021 di distrik Burzyansky dekat danau Yylkysykkan didirikan monumen setinggi lima meter (kudanya sendiri 3,5 meter) yang dicor di pengecoran Kasl.
claim.en: In 2021 a five-metre monument (the horse itself 3.5 metres) cast at the Kasli foundry was set up in the Burzyansky district near Lake Yylkysykkan.

claims_provenance.quote: En 2021, dans le district de Burzyansky, près du lac Yylkysykkan, un monument de cinq mètres de haut (le cheval lui-même y mesure 3,5 mètres) a été coulé à la fonderie de fer Kasl.

short_description.id: Badraç adalah naga berkepala tujuh dalam mitologi Turk yang menyemburkan api, bersisik seperti zirah, dan hanya mati bila ketujuh kepalanya dipenggal.
short_description.en: Badraç is the seven-headed dragon of Turkic mythology: fire-breathing, armoured in scales, and killed only when all seven of its heads are cut off.

long_description.id:
Dalam mitologi Turk, Badraç atau Padraç adalah naga berkepala tujuh. Ia menyemburkan api dari mulutnya, ekornya melecut seperti cambuk, dan kulitnya dilapisi sisik sekuat baju zirah. Karakurt mencatat bentuk nama lain seperti Badraş, Batraç, dan Padraş.

Untuk membunuhnya, ketujuh kepalanya harus dipenggal; kalau tidak, kepala yang terpotong tumbuh lagi. Menurut sebagian legenda, kepala yang dipenggal satu per satu kembali ke tempatnya, sehingga ketujuhnya harus dipotong bersamaan. Karakurt menafsirkan banyaknya kepala sebagai lambang memiliki lebih dari satu nyawa.

Salah satu sumber menyoroti bahwa gagasan naga muncul dengan berbagai nama di hampir setiap masyarakat. Sebagian orang bahkan menunjuk kalender Turk 12 hewan, yang menamai satu tahun dengan naga, sebagai petunjuk bahwa manusia pernah menyaksikan makhluk semacam itu.
long_description.en:
In Turkic mythology Badraç or Padraç is a seven-headed dragon. It spews fire from its mouth, its tail cracks like a whip, and its hide is covered in scales as strong as armour. Karakurt records other forms of the name such as Badraş, Batraç and Padraş.

To kill it, all seven heads must be cut off; otherwise a severed head grows back. In some legends heads cut off one at a time return to their place, so all seven must be cut at once. Karakurt interprets the many heads as a sign of having more than one life.

One source notes that the dragon idea appears under various names in almost every society. Some even point to the 12-animal Turkic calendar, which names a year after the dragon, as a hint that humans once witnessed such a creature.

short_description.id: Ular Berbulu adalah dewa atau sosok supernatural penting dalam banyak agama Mesoamerika, dikenal sebagai Quetzalcōātl oleh orang Aztek dan Kukulkan oleh Maya Yukatek.
short_description.en: The Feathered Serpent is a prominent deity or supernatural entity of many Mesoamerican religions, known as Quetzalcōātl to the Aztecs and Kukulkan to the Yucatec Maya.

long_description.id:
Ular Berbulu adalah sosok ilahi yang dipuja dalam banyak agama Mesoamerika. Orang Aztek menyebutnya Quetzalcōātl, Maya Yukatek menyebutnya Kukulkan, dan Maya Kʼicheʼ mengenalnya sebagai Qʼuqʼumatz dan Tohil. Bulunya ditafsirkan sebagai lambang sifat ilahi dan kemampuan terbang, sedangkan tubuh ularnya sebagai lambang sifat manusiawi yang melata di bumi.

Gambar ular berbulu sudah muncul dalam kebudayaan Olmek (sekitar 1400–400 SM), biasanya berupa ular derik berjambul. Di Teotihuacan (200 SM – 700 M) sosok ini menonjol di Kuil Ular Berbulu, dan secara umum paling sering tampil dalam arsitektur Mesoamerika.

Menurut legenda, Ular Berbulu menguasai bintang pagi, menciptakan buku dan kalender, serta memberi jagung kepada manusia. Ia juga melambangkan kematian dan kelahiran kembali, dan menjadi pelindung para pendeta.
long_description.en:
The Feathered Serpent is a divine figure revered in many Mesoamerican religions. The Aztecs called it Quetzalcōātl, the Yucatec Maya Kukulkan, and the Kʼicheʼ Maya knew it as Qʼuqʼumatz and Tohil. Its feathers are read as a sign of divine nature and flight, its serpent body as a sign of a human nature that creeps on the earth.

Images of feathered serpents already appear in Olmec culture (c. 1400–400 BC), usually as a crested rattlesnake. At Teotihuacan (200 BC – 700 AD) the figure is prominent on the Temple of the Feathered Serpent, and overall it appears most often in Mesoamerican architecture.

According to legend, the Feathered Serpent rules the morning star, invented books and the calendar, and gave maize to humanity. It also stands for death and rebirth and is the patron of priests.

Orang Aztek menyebutnya Quetzalcōātl, Maya Yukatek menyebutnya Kukulkan, dan Maya Kʼicheʼ mengenalnya sebagai Qʼuqʼumatz dan Tohil. Bulunya ditafsirkan sebagai lambang sifat ilahi dan kemampuan terbang, sedangkan tubuh ularnya sebagai lambang sifat manusiawi yang melata di bumi.
long_description.en: The Feathered Serpent is a divine figure revered in many Mesoamerican religions. The Aztecs called it Quetzalcōātl, the Yucatec Maya Kukulkan, and the Kʼicheʼ Maya knew it as Qʼuqʼumatz and Tohil. Its feathers are read as a sign of divine nature and flight, its serpent body as a sign of a human nature that creeps on the earth.

long_description.id: Gambar ular berbulu sudah muncul dalam kebudayaan Olmek (sekitar 1400–400 SM), biasanya berupa ular derik berjambul. Di Teotihuacan (200 SM – 700 M) sosok ini menonjol di Kuil Ular Berbulu, dan secara umum paling sering tampil dalam arsitektur Mesoamerika.
long_description.en: Images of feathered serpents already appear in Olmec culture (c. 1400–400 BC), usually as a crested rattlesnake. At Teotihuacan (200 BC – 700 AD) the figure is prominent on the Temple of the Feathered Serpent, and overall it appears most often in Mesoamerican architecture.

long_description.id: Menurut legenda, Ular Berbulu menguasai bintang pagi, menciptakan buku dan kalender, serta memberi jagung kepada manusia. Ia juga melambangkan kematian dan kelahiran kembali, dan menjadi pelindung para pendeta.
long_description.en: According to legend, the Feathered Serpent rules the morning star, invented books and the calendar, and gave maize to humanity. It also stands for death and rebirth and is the patron of priests.

short_description.id: Naga Rhodes adalah naga legenda yang meneror pulau Rhodes pada 1340-an sampai dibunuh ksatria Hospitaller Dieudonné de Gozon.
short_description.en: The dragon of Rhodes is a legendary dragon that terrorised Rhodes in the 1340s until killed by the Hospitaller knight Dieudonné de Gozon.

long_description.id:
Naga Rhodes menurut legenda meneror lembah Soudourli di kaki gunung Santo Stefanus pada 1340-an, masa kekuasaan Ordo Hospitaller. Korbannya begitu banyak sehingga Grand Master Hélion de Villeneuve melarang para ksatria melawannya. Menurut Bosio naga itu sebesar kuda, berkepala ular, bertelinga bagal bersisik, dan bergigi tajam.

Ksatria Dieudonné de Gozon melanggar larangan itu: ia berlatih dengan naga kayu berengsel, kembali sekitar 1342 bersama dua anjing besar, membunuh naga itu, dan memasang kepalanya di benteng. Legenda serupa sudah ada di Kos sejak 1420, dan sebagian sarjana menduga kisah ini berawal dari hewan nyata.
long_description.en:
The dragon of Rhodes is said to have terrorised the Soudourli valley at the foot of Mount Saint Stephen in the 1340s, under the Knights Hospitaller. It claimed so many victims that Grand Master Hélion de Villeneuve forbade the knights to fight it. Bosio describes it as the size of a horse, with a serpent's head, scaly mule's ears and sharp teeth.

The knight Dieudonné de Gozon defied the ban: he trained with an articulated wooden dragon, returned around 1342 with two mastiffs, killed the dragon and set its head on the walls. A similar legend existed on Kos from 1420, and some scholars think the story stems from a real animal.

short_description.id: Zaldi, "kuda", adalah roh berwujud kuda dalam mitologi Basque, wujud yang diambil penyihir dan Mari, termasuk kuda putih tanpa kepala yang menandakan kematian.
short_description.en: Zaldi, 'horse', is a horse-shaped spirit of Basque mythology, a form taken by witches and by Mari, including the headless white horse that foretells death.

long_description.id:
Zaldi, "kuda" dalam bahasa Basque, adalah irelu atau roh dalam legenda Basque. Kuda adalah salah satu wujud yang diambil para penyihir (sorginak) dan juga dewi Mari, dan sejumlah roh bawah tanah digambarkan berwujud kuda. Dari gua Laxarrigibel dekat Tardets keluar makhluk berupa kuda putih yang pernah menyekap seorang pemuda.

Zamari zuria, kuda putih tanpa kepala di pegunungan Basque, menandakan kematian; di Soule dan Gipuzkoa ia diperankan penari sebagai roh serealia. Dalam legenda Obantzun, kuda betina hitam membawa seorang pelayan ke jurang dan ia tak kembali. Tokoh Zamaltzain dalam maskarade Zuberoa memakai kostum kuda.
long_description.en:
Zaldi, Basque for 'horse', is an irelu or spirit of Basque legend. The horse is one of the forms taken by the witches (sorginak) and by the goddess Mari, and some underground spirits appear as horses. From the Laxarrigibel cave near Tardets comes a white-horse being that once held a young man captive.

Zamari zuria, a headless white horse of the Basque mountains, foretells death; in Soule and Gipuzkoa a dancer plays it as the cereal spirit. In the Obantzun legend a black mare carries a servant girl into a chasm and she never returns. The Zamaltzain of the Zuberoa masquerades wears a horse costume.

short_description.id: Zaldi, "kuda", adalah roh berwujud kuda dalam mitologi Basque, wujud yang diambil penyihir dan Mari, termasuk kuda putih tanpa kepala yang menandakan kematian.
short_description.en: Zaldi, 'horse', is a horse-shaped spirit of Basque mythology, a form taken by witches and by Mari, including the headless white horse that foretells death.

long_description.id: Zaldi, "kuda" dalam bahasa Basque, adalah irelu atau roh dalam legenda Basque. Kuda adalah salah satu wujud yang diambil para penyihir (sorginak) dan juga dewi Mari, dan sejumlah roh bawah tanah digambarkan berwujud kuda. Dari gua Laxarrigibel dekat Tardets keluar makhluk berupa kuda putih yang pernah menyekap seorang pemuda.
long_description.en: Zaldi, Basque for 'horse', is an irelu or spirit of Basque legend. The horse is one of the forms taken by the witches (sorginak) and by the goddess Mari, and some underground spirits appear as horses. From the Laxarrigibel cave near Tardets comes a white-horse being that once held a young man captive.

long_description.id: Zamari zuria, kuda putih tanpa kepala di pegunungan Basque, menandakan kematian; di Soule dan Gipuzkoa ia diperankan penari sebagai roh serealia. Dalam legenda Obantzun, kuda betina hitam membawa seorang pelayan ke jurang dan ia tak kembali. Tokoh Zamaltzain dalam maskarade Zuberoa memakai kostum kuda.
long_description.en: Zamari zuria, a headless white horse of the Basque mountains, foretells death; in Soule and Gipuzkoa a dancer plays it as the cereal spirit. In the Obantzun legend a black mare carries a servant girl into a chasm and she never returns. The Zamaltzain of the Zuberoa masquerades wears a horse costume.

short_description.id: Chudo-Yudo adalah tokoh dongeng rakyat Rusia yang sering bersifat ikan; dalam satu dongeng terkenal ia berupa sekelompok ular berkepala banyak yang membakar kota dan desa.
short_description.en: Chudo-Yudo is a character of Russian folk tales that often has fish-like traits; in one famous tale it is a group of many-headed serpents that burn towns and villages.

long_description.id:
Chudo-Yudo, juga disebut "keajaiban laut", adalah tokoh dongeng rakyat Rusia yang sering memiliki ciri dan sifat ikan. Para etnografer dan ahli budaya belum sepakat tentang asal-usul tokoh ini.

Dalam dongeng "Ivan, Anak Petani, dan Chudo-Yudo", Chudo-Yudo adalah sekelompok ular berkepala enam, sembilan, dan dua belas yang tinggal di seberang Sungai Smorodina dan menyeberang lewat Jembatan Kalinov. Ia digambarkan menunggang kuda dan membakar kota serta desa. Chudo-Yudo berkepala dua belas punya jari berapi yang dapat menumbuhkan kembali kepala yang terpenggal. Ia tinggal di istana batu bersama istri-istri penyihir dan ibu ularnya, dan lawan utamanya adalah Ivan, anak petani.

A. N. Afanasyev mencatat bahwa dalam beberapa versi dongeng tentang Raja Laut, peran sang raja diberikan kepada ular, setan, atau Chudo-Yudo yang durjana, dan menurutnya nama Chudo-Yudo kebanyakan diberikan kepada ular mitis, yaitu naga-awan. Max Vasmer menganggap "yudo" kemungkinan besar hanya bentukan berima dari kata "chudo".
long_description.en:
Chudo-Yudo, also called the "sea wonder", is a character of Russian folk tales that often has the traits and nature of a fish. Ethnographers and cultural scholars have not agreed on the origin of the figure.

In the tale "Ivan the Peasant's Son and Chudo-Yudo", Chudo-Yudo is a group of six-, nine- and twelve-headed serpents living beyond the River Smorodina and crossing by the Kalinov Bridge. It is shown riding a horse and burning towns and villages. The twelve-headed Chudo-Yudo has a fiery finger that regrows severed heads. It lives in stone chambers with sorceress wives and a serpent mother, and its chief opponent is Ivan, the peasant's son.

A. N. Afanasyev noted that in some versions of the tale of the Sea King the king's role passes to a serpent, the devil or the lawless Chudo-Yudo, and in his view the name Chudo-Yudo is mostly given to the mythical serpent, the dragon-cloud. Max Vasmer thought "yudo" most likely just a rhyming formation modelled on "chudo".

claim.id: Chudo-Yudo (Чудо-юдо, "keajaiban laut") adalah tokoh dongeng rakyat Rusia yang sering berciri ikan; etnografer dan ahli budaya belum sepakat tentang asal-usulnya.
claim.en: Chudo-Yudo ("sea wonder") is a Russian folk-tale character often with fish traits; ethnographers and cultural scholars have not agreed on its origin.

claims_provenance.quote: Чудо-юдо (чудо морское) — персонаж русских народных сказок, часто обладающий чертами и свойствами рыбы. Единого мнения о происхождении персонажа в работах этнографов и культурологов на сегодняшний день не сложилось.

claim.id: Menurut A. N. Afanasyev, dalam versi lain dongeng Raja Laut dan putrinya yang bijak, peran Raja Laut diberikan kepada ular, setan, dan Chudo-Yudo yang durjana.
claim.en: According to A. N. Afanasyev, in other versions of the tale of the Sea King and his wise daughter the Sea King's role passes to a serpent, the devil and the lawless Chudo-Yudo.

claims_provenance.quote: в одном варианте народной сказки о Морском Царе и его вещей дочери Морской Царь прямо назван Окиан-море; в других же списках роль его передаётся змею, чёрту и беззаконному Чуду-Юду.

claim.en: According to Afanasyev, the name Chudo-Yudo is mostly given to the mythical serpent, the dragon-cloud.

claims_provenance.quote: Название Чудо-Юдо, согласно Афанасьеву, подтверждает ту же мысль: оно большею частью придаётся мифическому змею (дракону-туче).

claims_provenance.quote: Макс Фасмер считал наиболее вероятным, что юдо — «всего лишь рифмованное образование по образцу слова чудо»

claim.id: Dalam dongeng "Ivan, Anak Petani, dan Chudo-Yudo", Chudo-Yudo adalah sekelompok ular berkepala 6, 9, dan 12 (enam, sembilan, dua belas) yang jahat, tinggal di seberang Sungai Smorodina dan menyeberang lewat Jembatan Kalinov, digambarkan menunggang kuda, dan membakar kota serta desa.
claim.en: In the tale "Ivan the Peasant's Son and Chudo-Yudo", Chudo-Yudo is a group of evil 6-, 9- and 12-headed serpents living beyond the River Smorodina, crossing by the Kalinov Bridge, shown on horseback, burning towns and villages.

claims_provenance.quote: В русской народной сказке «Иван — крестьянский сын и Чудо-юдо» Чудо-юдо — это группа многоголовых (6-, 9-, 12-головых) змеев, отрицательных персонажей. Живут они за рекой Смородиной, через которую перебираются по Калинову мосту. В сказке Чудо-юдо изображается верхом на коне. Вред от него заключается в том, что оно сжигает города-сёла огнём.

claim.id: Chudo-Yudo berkepala 12 (dua belas) punya jari berapi yang dapat menumbuhkan kembali kepala yang terpenggal.
claim.en: The 12-headed (twelve-headed) Chudo-Yudo has a fiery finger that regrows severed heads.

claims_provenance.quote: 12-головое Чудо-юдо обладает огненным пальцем, который позволяет регенерировать срубленные головы.

claim.id: Chudo-Yudo tinggal di istana batu bersama istri-istri penyihir dan ibu ularnya; lawan utamanya adalah Ivan, anak petani.
claim.en: Chudo-Yudo lives in stone chambers with sorceress wives and a serpent mother; its chief opponent is Ivan, the peasant's son.

claims_provenance.quote: Живёт чудо-юдо в каменных палатах, где у чуда-юда есть жёны-колдуньи и мать-змеиха. Главный противник чуда-юда, как и следует из названия сказки, — Иван — крестьянский сын.

Afanasyev mencatat bahwa dalam beberapa versi dongeng tentang Raja Laut, peran sang raja diberikan kepada ular, setan, atau Chudo-Yudo yang durjana, dan menurutnya nama Chudo-Yudo kebanyakan diberikan kepada ular mitis, yaitu naga-awan. Max Vasmer menganggap "yudo" kemungkinan besar hanya bentukan berima dari kata "chudo".
long_description.en: A. N. Afanasyev noted that in some versions of the tale of the Sea King the king's role passes to a serpent, the devil or the lawless Chudo-Yudo, and in his view the name Chudo-Yudo is mostly given to the mythical serpent, the dragon-cloud. Max Vasmer thought "yudo" most likely just a rhyming formation modelled on "chudo".

short_description.id: Faronika adalah ikan atau ular air dalam cerita rakyat Slovenia yang memikul bumi di punggungnya; geraknya menyebabkan gempa.
short_description.en: Faronika is a fish or water serpent of Slovene folklore that carries the earth on its back; its movements cause earthquakes.

long_description.id:
Faronika adalah ikan atau ular air dalam cerita rakyat Slovenia yang memikul bumi di punggungnya. Gerakannya menyebabkan gempa bumi, dan bila ia menyelam, dunia akan berakhir. Ikan atau ular yang terkait samudra kosmis adalah motif umum dalam banyak kosmologi mitis.

Namanya berasal dari Firaun dalam Alkitab yang tenggelam di Laut Merah, yang menurut kepercayaan rakyat Slovenia berubah menjadi ikan. Orang Slovenia dari Zámuří justru mengenal dua ikan yang berputar di air mengelilingi bumi dan menimbulkan gempa saat menggesek atau memukulnya dengan ekor.

Kisah Faronika kemudian bercampur dengan legenda Veronika dari Mali Grad dekat Kamnik, yang karena ketamakannya diubah menjadi setengah perempuan setengah ular. Ikan Faronika juga muncul dalam kisah Slavia lama tentang penciptaan dunia yang terkait Kekristenan, saat yang ada hanyalah Tuhan, Matahari, dan laut.
long_description.en:
Faronika is a fish or water serpent of Slovene folklore that carries the earth on its back. Its movements cause earthquakes, and if it dives the world will end. A fish or serpent linked to the cosmic ocean is a common motif in many mythical cosmologies.

Its name comes from the biblical Pharaoh who drowned in the Red Sea and, according to Slovene folk belief, turned into a fish. Slovenes from Zámuří instead know two fish circling the earth in the waters, causing earthquakes when they rub against it or strike it with their tails.

The tale of Faronika later merged with the legend of Veronika of Mali Grad near Kamnik, who was turned into half woman, half snake for her greed. The fish Faronika also appears in an Old Slavic, Christian-linked story of the creation of the world, when only God, the Sun and the sea existed.

short_description.id: Kuperan adalah raksasa (Riese) dalam lingkaran kisah Siegfried pembunuh naga, pemegang kunci gunung tempat seekor naga tinggal.
short_description.en: Kuperan is a giant (Riese) in the cycle of tales about Siegfried the dragon-slayer, keeper of the key to a mountain where a dragon lives.

long_description.id:
Kuperan adalah raksasa (Riese) dalam lingkaran kisah Siegfried pembunuh naga (Drachentöter), yang memegang kunci masuk ke sebuah gunung tempat naga bersarang. Dalam puisi tentang Seyfrid, Siegfried berusaha membebaskan putri Kriemhild yang ditawan naga, dibantu kurcaci Eugel serta raksasa Kuperan yang enggan dan berkhianat.

Eugel memberi tahu Siegfried bahwa raksasa Kuperan tinggal di dekat situ dan memegang kunci gunung. Mereka bertarung, dan Siegfried mengampuni raksasa yang terluka itu dengan syarat ia membantu membebaskan Kriemhild. long_description.en:
Kuperan is a giant (Riese) in the cycle of tales about Siegfried the dragon-slayer (Drachentöter), holding the key that opens a mountain where a dragon lairs. In the poem about Seyfrid, Siegfried sets out to free the princess Kriemhild held by the dragon, helped by the dwarf Eugel and by the unwilling, treacherous giant Kuperan.

Eugel tells Siegfried that the giant Kuperan lives nearby and holds the key to the mountain. They fight, and Siegfried spares the wounded giant on condition that he help free Kriemhild. But in the forest Kuperan strikes Siegfried senseless, and Eugel covers the hero with his cloak of invisibility. Kuperan later reveals a sword able to defeat the dragon, yet attacks again; this time Siegfried pushes him off the rock and he shatters into pieces. The de article says Kuperan betrayed him twice, while the en summary speaks of a third attack.

short_description.id: Heqet adalah dewi kesuburan Mesir yang digambarkan sebagai katak.
short_description.en: Heqet is an Egyptian fertility goddess depicted as a frog.

long_description.id:
Heqet adalah dewi kesuburan Mesir yang digambarkan sebagai katak. Katak berkaitan dengan banjir tahunan Nil dan kesuburan.

Kultusnya diketahui setidaknya sejak masa Dinasti Awal. Ia dianggap sebagai istri Khnum yang membentuk tubuh anak dengan roda tembikar. Dalam mitos Osiris ia memberikan napas hidup kepada Horus saat lahir. Sumber pendamping menggambarkannya sebagai katak atau perempuan berkepala katak.
long_description.en:
Heqet is an Egyptian fertility goddess depicted as a frog. The frog is linked with the annual Nile flood and fertility.

Her cult is known from at least the Early Dynastic Period. She is regarded as wife of Khnum, who shapes children’s bodies on a potter’s wheel. In the Osiris myth she breathes life into Horus at birth. The accompanying source depicts her as a frog or frog-headed woman.

claims_provenance.quote: Heqet (Egyptian ḥqt, also ḥqtyt "Heqtit"), sometimes spelled Heket, is an Egyptian goddess of fertility, identified with Hathor, represented in the form of a frog.

claim.id: Katak berkaitan dengan banjir tahunan Nil dan kesuburan.
claim.en: The frog is linked with the annual Nile flood and fertility.

claims_provenance.quote:
To the Egyptians, the frog was an ancient symbol of fertility, related to the annual flooding of the Nile. 
Heqet was originally the female counterpart of Khnum, or the wife of Khnum, and eventually she also became the mother of Heru-ur.
It has been proposed that her name is the origin of the name of Hecate, the Greek goddess of witchcraft.

claim.id: Kultusnya diketahui setidaknya sejak masa Dinasti Awal.
claim.en: Her cult is known from at least the Early Dynastic Period.

claims_provenance.quote: The beginning of her cult dates to the Early Dynastic Period at least. Her name was part of the names of some high-born Second Dynasty individuals buried at Helwan, such as prince Nisuheqet, and was mentioned on a stela of Wepemnofret and in the Pyramid Texts. Early frog statuettes are often thought to be depictions of her.

claim.id: Ia dianggap sebagai istri Khnum yang membentuk tubuh anak dengan roda tembikar.
claim.en: She is regarded as wife of Khnum, who shapes children’s bodies on a potter’s wheel.

claim.id: Dalam mitos Osiris ia memberikan napas hidup kepada Horus saat lahir.
claim.en: In the Osiris myth she breathes life into Horus at birth.

claims_provenance.quote: In the Osiris myth, it was Heqet who breathed life into the new body of Horus at birth, as she was a goddess of the last moments of birth. As the birth of Horus became more intimately associated with the resurrection of Osiris, so Heqet's role became one more closely associated with resurrection.

short_description.id: Taweret adalah dewi Mesir pelindung kelahiran dan kesuburan.
short_description.en: Taweret is an Egyptian goddess protecting childbirth and fertility.

long_description.id:
Taweret adalah dewi Mesir pelindung kelahiran dan kesuburan. Namanya berarti Yang Agung.

Ia berupa kuda nil betina berkaki dua dengan unsur singa dan buaya. Ia dekat dengan dewi kuda nil Ipet, Reret, dan Hedjet. Gambarnya menghiasi pisau atau tongkat magis untuk ritual perlindungan bayi. Taweret juga disebut pasangan Bes dalam sumber pendamping.
long_description.en:
Taweret is an Egyptian goddess protecting childbirth and fertility. Her name means the Great One.

She takes the form of a bipedal female hippopotamus with lion and crocodile features. She is closely associated with the hippopotamus goddesses Ipet, Reret and Hedjet. Her image adorns magical knives or wands used in infant-protection rites. Taweret is also called Bes’s consort in the accompanying source.

short_description.id: Leucrota (leucrocuta) adalah hewan dongeng (fabeldier) keturunan crocotta yang dapat meniru suara manusia dan bergigi tulang utuh.
short_description.en: The leucrota (leucrocuta) is a fabulous beast (fabeldier) descended from the crocotta that can imitate human voices and has solid bone in place of teeth.

long_description.id:
Leucrota (leucrocuta) adalah hewan dongeng (fabeldier), keturunan crocotta dengan hewan lain. Seperti crocotta yang mirip anjing, ia dapat meniru suara manusia, tetapi tubuhnya mirip antilop dengan kuku belah dan sangat cepat. Ia berpaha babi hutan (zwijn), berekor, berdada, dan berleher singa, serta berkepala luak; sebagai ganti gigi ia memiliki sisir tulang yang menghancurkan segalanya. Leucrota tidak pernah menutup mata, dan tulang punggungnya begitu kaku sehingga ia harus berbalik badan untuk melihat ke belakang.

Plinius menulis tentang leucrocotta, makhluk mirip hiena yang disebutnya hewan tercepat, sebesar keledai, berpaha rusa, berleher, berekor, dan berdada singa, berkepala luak, berkuku belah, bermulut terbuka sampai telinga, dan bertulang sebagai ganti gigi, yang konon meniru suara manusia. Bestiari dari masa kemudian mencampuradukkan berbagai kisah ini; Aberdeen Bestiary menyebut Leucrota hewan cepat yang lahir di India.
long_description.en:
The leucrota (leucrocuta) is a fabulous beast (fabeldier), the offspring of the crocotta and another animal. Like the dog-like crocotta it can imitate a human voice, but it resembles an antelope with cloven hooves and great speed. It has the thighs of a boar (zwijn), the tail, breast and neck of a lion and the head of a badger; instead of teeth it has bony ridges that grind everything. The leucrota never closes its eyes, and its spine is so stiff that it must turn round to see what is behind it.

Pliny wrote of the leucrocotta, a hyena-like creature he called the fastest of all beasts: as big as an ass, with haunches like a stag, neck, tail and breast like a lion, a badger's head, split hooves, a mouth gaping back to the ears and ridges of bone where teeth should be, and reputed to mimic human voices. Later bestiaries of the Middle Ages muddled these accounts; the Aberdeen Bestiary calls the Leucrota a swift animal born in India.

short_description.id: Gizotso adalah manusia serigala mitologi Basque, monster setengah manusia setengah serigala yang tinggal di sekitar hutan dan muncul pada malam hari berbalut rantai.
short_description.en: Gizotso is the werewolf of Basque mythology, a half-man, half-wolf monster living near the woods and appearing at night laden with chains.

long_description.id:
Gizotso, dari gizon "manusia" dan otso "serigala", adalah manusia serigala Basque: monster setengah manusia setengah serigala yang tinggal di sekitar hutan dan muncul pada malam hari dengan rantai. Di Luzaide ia dipercaya sangat kuat, dan di Agiano dekat Zeanuri ia dianggap lahir dari hubungan binatang dan perempuan; di sana ia konon menyerang seorang perempuan yang bergegas pulang.

Sumber berbeda soal luka perempuan itu: payudaranya dirobek atau matanya dicungkil. Gizotso berbeda dari Otsoko, personifikasi serigala, dan Pierre de Lancre pada 1612 sudah menulis tentang "Monsieur La Forêt" yang meneror Pyrenees.
long_description.en:
Gizotso, from gizon 'man' and otso 'wolf', is the Basque werewolf: a half-man, half-wolf monster living around the woods and appearing at night in chains. At Luzaide it is thought immensely strong, and at Agiano near Zeanuri it is held to be born of a beast and a woman; there it reportedly attacked a woman hurrying home.

Sources differ on the woman's wounds: her breasts torn off or her eyes torn out. Gizotso is distinct from Otsoko, the personified wolf, and in 1612 Pierre de Lancre already wrote of a 'Monsieur La Forêt' haunting the Pyrenees.

Di Luzaide ia dipercaya sangat kuat, dan di Agiano dekat Zeanuri ia dianggap lahir dari hubungan binatang dan perempuan; di sana ia konon menyerang seorang perempuan yang bergegas pulang.
long_description.en: Gizotso, from gizon 'man' and otso 'wolf', is the Basque werewolf: a half-man, half-wolf monster living around the woods and appearing at night in chains. At Luzaide it is thought immensely strong, and at Agiano near Zeanuri it is held to be born of a beast and a woman; there it reportedly attacked a woman hurrying home.

long_description.en: Sources differ on the woman's wounds: her breasts torn off or her eyes torn out. Gizotso is distinct from Otsoko, the personified wolf, and in 1612 Pierre de Lancre already wrote of a 'Monsieur La Forêt' haunting the Pyrenees.
