short_description.id: Diyu adalah makhluk mitos dalam mitologi Tatar dan Bashkir: dalam ensiklopedia Bashkir ia digambarkan sebagai iblis jahat raksasa berkepala banyak yang tinggal di bawah tanah atau di bawah air.
short_description.en: Diyu is a mythical being of Tatar and Bashkir mythology; the Bashkir encyclopedia describes it as an evil many-headed giant demon living underground or under water.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi Tatar dan Bashkir, dию pәriләre (para diyu peri) termasuk makhluk mitos dengan derajat paling rendah. Menurut mitos Kazan, mereka tinggal di kota-kota mereka sendiri di bawah tanah dan di dasar laut. Sebagian mitos membagi mereka menjadi dua golongan, yaitu diyu dan peri (pәri).
long_description.en: In Tatar and Bashkir mythology the diyu peris are counted among the lowest-ranking mythical beings. According to the myths of the the people of Kazan they lived in their own cities underground and on the sea floor. Some myths divide them into two kinds, the diyu and the peri (pәri).

long_description.id: Di permukaan bumi mereka dipercaya tidak kasatmata dan hanya menampakkan diri kepada manusia dalam rupa manusia. Dengan menjelma menjadi gadis cantik, mereka bisa menikah dengan manusia. Mereka juga menjamu orang dengan aneka makanan, tetapi bila makanan itu disantap sambil mengucap bismillah, konon makanan itu berubah menjadi kotoran kuda.
long_description.en: On the earth's surface they were believed to be invisible, showing themselves to people only in human form. By turning into a beautiful girl they could marry humans. They also treated people to all sorts of food, but if the food was eaten with the words bismillah, it is said to have turned into horse dung.

long_description.id: Ensiklopedia Bashkir menyebut diyu (дейеү) dalam mitologi Bashkir sebagai iblis jahat, raksasa berkepala banyak, yang berakar pada dew Iran. Ia biasanya berjenis kelamin laki-laki, lebih jarang perempuan, dan kerajaannya terletak di balik Kaf-tau, di langit, di bawah tanah, atau di bawah air.
long_description.en: The Bashkir encyclopedia calls the diyu (дейеү) of Bashkir mythology an evil demon and many-headed giant that goes back to the Iranian devs. It is usually male, more rarely female, and its realm lies beyond Kaf-tau, in the heavens, underground or under water.

long_description.id: Diyu dapat menjelma menjadi badai, perempuan tua, atau jarum. Ia memangsa atau menawan manusia, membawa lari ternak, serta menculik gadis lalu menikahinya. Kekuatannya bergantung pada jumlah kepalanya, yang bisa 3, 6, 9, atau 12, dan hanya seorang batyr yang mampu membinasakannya dengan memenggal kepala-kepalanya.
long_description.en: The diyu can turn into a storm, an old woman or a needle. It devours people or holds them captive, carries off livestock, and abducts girls to marry them. Its strength depends on the number of its heads, which may be 3, 6, 9 or 12, and only a batyr can destroy it by cutting off its heads.

long_description.id: Diyu muncul dalam epos Ural-batyr dan Akbuzat serta dalam dongeng. Pada tahun 1880 Kayum Nasıyri menelaah Diyü (Dev) bersama makhluk luar biasa lain yang sering muncul dalam dongeng rakyat Tatar.
long_description.en: The diyu appears in the epics Ural-batyr and Akbuzat and in folk tales. In 1880 Kayum Nasıyri analysed the Diyü (Dev) alongside other extraordinary creatures common in Tatar folk tales.

short_description.id: Valkyrie adalah kelompok perempuan ilahi dalam mitologi yang memilih pejuang gugur untuk dibawa ke Valhalla milik Odin.
short_description.en: Valkyries are divine women of Norse myth who select fallen warriors and bring them to Odin's Valhalla.

long_description.id:
Valkyrie berarti pemilih yang gugur. Mereka digambarkan sebagai perempuan pejuang yang menunggang kuda, serigala, atau babi hutan dan bersenjatakan tombak. Dalam tugas Odin mereka menentukan nasib pejuang dan membawa yang terpilih ke Valhalla. Museum Denmark juga menyebut mereka makhluk ilahi perempuan.

Menurut satu uraian, Freyja memilih separuh yang gugur untuk Fólkvangr dan Valkyrie memilih separuh lainnya bagi Odin. Mereka juga melayani pejuang terpilih di Valhalla, yang kelak bertempur di sisi Odin saat Ragnarök. Kisah mereka terdapat dalam Prose Edda dan Poetic Edda.

Tradisi juga mengaitkan Valkyrie dengan gagak dan kisah gadis angsa. Jumlah mereka beragam menurut sumber. Brynhild adalah Valkyrie terkenal yang, setelah menentang Odin, dibuat fana dan ditidurkan dalam lingkaran api. Istilah sejenis juga dikenal di England kuno.
long_description.en:
Valkyrie means chooser of the slain. They are depicted as armed warrior women riding horses, wolves or boars. In Odin's service they decide warriors' fates and lead the chosen to Valhalla. A museum also calls them female divinities.

In one account Freyja selects half of the dead for Fólkvangr and Valkyries choose the rest for Odin. They serve the chosen warriors at Valhalla, where those warriors prepare to fight beside Odin at Ragnarök. Their stories appear in the Prose Edda and Poetic Edda.

Tradition also links Valkyries with ravens and swan maidens. Their number varies across accounts. Brynhild is a famous Valkyrie made mortal and put to sleep within a ring of fire after defying Odin. A related name was known in England.

short_description.id: Valkyrie adalah kelompok perempuan ilahi dalam mitologi yang memilih pejuang gugur untuk dibawa ke Valhalla milik Odin.
short_description.en: Valkyries are divine women of Norse myth who select fallen warriors and bring them to Odin's Valhalla.

long_description.id: Valkyrie berarti pemilih yang gugur. Mereka digambarkan sebagai perempuan pejuang yang menunggang kuda, serigala, atau babi hutan dan bersenjatakan tombak. Dalam tugas Odin mereka menentukan nasib pejuang dan membawa yang terpilih ke Valhalla. Museum Denmark juga menyebut mereka makhluk ilahi perempuan.
long_description.en: Valkyrie means chooser of the slain. They are depicted as armed warrior women riding horses, wolves or boars. In Odin's service they decide warriors' fates and lead the chosen to Valhalla. A museum also calls them female divinities.

long_description.id: Menurut satu uraian, Freyja memilih separuh yang gugur untuk Fólkvangr dan Valkyrie memilih separuh lainnya bagi Odin. Mereka juga melayani pejuang terpilih di Valhalla, yang kelak bertempur di sisi Odin saat Ragnarök. Kisah mereka terdapat dalam Prose Edda dan Poetic Edda.
long_description.en: In one account Freyja selects half of the dead for Fólkvangr and Valkyries choose the rest for Odin. They serve the chosen warriors at Valhalla, where those warriors prepare to fight beside Odin at Ragnarök. Their stories appear in the Prose Edda and Poetic Edda.

long_description.id: Tradisi juga mengaitkan Valkyrie dengan gagak dan kisah gadis angsa. Jumlah mereka beragam menurut sumber. Brynhild adalah Valkyrie terkenal yang, setelah menentang Odin, dibuat fana dan ditidurkan dalam lingkaran api. Istilah sejenis juga dikenal di England kuno.
long_description.en: Tradition also links Valkyries with ravens and swan maidens. Their number varies across accounts. Brynhild is a famous Valkyrie made mortal and put to sleep within a ring of fire after defying Odin. A related name was known in England.

short_description.id: Gargouille atau Goji adalah monster naga legendaris di kawasan Rouen yang ditaklukkan oleh Saint Romanus.
short_description.en: Gargouille or Goji is a legendary dragon from the area around Rouen subdued by Saint Romanus.

long_description.id:
Dalam cerita rakyat di Rouen, La Gargouille digambarkan sebagai naga berleher panjang dengan sayap mirip kelelawar serta kemampuan mengembuskan api. Monster ini berwujud seperti ular raksasa yang mendiami rawa-rawa di tepi sungai Seine dan memangsa manusia serta ternak.

Saint Romain menaklukkan monster tersebut menggunakan salib dan bantuan seorang terpidana mati yang menuntunnya kembali ke kota untuk dibakar. Karena kepala dan lehernya kebal terhadap api akibat semburannya sendiri, kepalanya dipajang di dinding katedral dan menjadi cikal bakal tradisi pelepasan tahanan.
long_description.en:
In lore around Rouen, La Gargouille is described as a dragon possessing a long neck, bat-like wings, and fiery breath. The beast lived as an enormous serpent in marshes along the Seine, preying upon people and beasts.

Saint Romanus subdued the monster using a crucifix alongside a condemned man who led it into the city to be burned. Because its head and neck were tempered against flames by fire breath, they were mounted upon cathedral walls, establishing the procession privilege.

short_description.id: Hippogriff adalah makhluk setengah elang setengah kuda yang diciptakan Ludovico Ariosto dalam Orlando Furioso sebagai anak griffin dan kuda betina, tunggangan yang dapat terbang ke Bulan.
short_description.en: The hippogriff is a half-eagle, half-horse creature invented by Ludovico Ariosto in Orlando Furioso as the offspring of a griffin and a mare, a steed that can fly to the Moon.

long_description.id:
Hippogriff atau hippogryph, dari bahasa Yunani híppos, "kuda", dan bahasa Italia grifo, "griffin", adalah makhluk bertubuh depan elang dan belakang kuda. Ludovico Ariosto menciptakannya pada awal abad ke-16 dalam Orlando Furioso sebagai anak griffin dan kuda betina, gabungan yang dianggap mustahil karena griffin memangsa kuda. Hippogriff milik penyihir Atlantes lalu ditunggangi Ruggiero untuk membebaskan Angelica, dan dapat terbang mengelilingi dunia sampai ke Bulan.

Kata ini masuk bahasa Inggris sebelum 1615, Gustave Doré sering menggambarnya pada abad ke-19, dan kini ia dikenal lewat Buckbeak dalam Harry Potter.
long_description.en:
The hippogriff or hippogryph, from Greek híppos, 'horse', and Italian grifo, 'griffin', has an eagle's front and a horse's hindquarters. Ludovico Ariosto invented it early in the 16th century in Orlando Furioso as the offspring of a griffin and a mare, a cross thought impossible since griffins prey on horses. Owned by the sorcerer Atlantes and then ridden by Ruggiero to free Angelica, it can fly round the world and to the Moon.

The word entered English before 1615, Gustave Doré often drew it in the 19th century, and today it is known through Buckbeak in Harry Potter.

short_description.id: Hippogriff adalah makhluk setengah elang setengah kuda yang diciptakan Ludovico Ariosto dalam Orlando Furioso sebagai anak griffin dan kuda betina, tunggangan yang dapat terbang ke Bulan.
short_description.en: The hippogriff is a half-eagle, half-horse creature invented by Ludovico Ariosto in Orlando Furioso as the offspring of a griffin and a mare, a steed that can fly to the Moon.

long_description.id: Hippogriff atau hippogryph, dari bahasa Yunani híppos, "kuda", dan bahasa Italia grifo, "griffin", adalah makhluk bertubuh depan elang dan belakang kuda. Ludovico Ariosto menciptakannya pada awal abad ke-16 dalam Orlando Furioso sebagai anak griffin dan kuda betina, gabungan yang dianggap mustahil karena griffin memangsa kuda. Hippogriff milik penyihir Atlantes lalu ditunggangi Ruggiero untuk membebaskan Angelica, dan dapat terbang mengelilingi dunia sampai ke Bulan.
long_description.en: The hippogriff or hippogryph, from Greek híppos, 'horse', and Italian grifo, 'griffin', has an eagle's front and a horse's hindquarters. Ludovico Ariosto invented it early in the 16th century in Orlando Furioso as the offspring of a griffin and a mare, a cross thought impossible since griffins prey on horses. Owned by the sorcerer Atlantes and then ridden by Ruggiero to free Angelica, it can fly round the world and to the Moon.

long_description.id: Kata ini masuk bahasa Inggris sebelum 1615, Gustave Doré sering menggambarnya pada abad ke-19, dan kini ia dikenal lewat Buckbeak dalam Harry Potter.
long_description.en: The word entered English before 1615, Gustave Doré often drew it in the 19th century, and today it is known through Buckbeak in Harry Potter.

short_description.id: Kelenken adalah iblis (demon) dalam mitologi suku Tehuelche di Patagonia, pembawa rasa sakit dan penyakit yang digambarkan sebagai burung pemangsa raksasa.
short_description.en: Kelenken is a demon in the mythology of the Tehuelche of Patagonia, a bringer of pain and disease pictured as a giant bird of prey.

long_description.id:
Kelenken adalah iblis (demon) dalam mitologi suku Tehuelche, penduduk asli Patagonia (Patagonië). Ia dipandang sebagai pembawa rasa sakit dan penyakit dan digambarkan sebagai burung pemangsa raksasa.

Menurut orang Tehuelche, malam (Tons) adalah ibu legendaris roh-roh jahat. Ketika matahari dan bulan bertemu, malam cepat menutupi bumi, dan ketika keduanya berpisah malam meninggalkan bumi lagi. Dari situ lahirlah tiga bersaudara: Axshem, pembawa rasa sakit; Maip, pembawa ketakutan dan kemalangan; dan Kelenken.

Nama Kelenken dipakai untuk genus burung teror (phorusrhacid) yang punah dari Patagonia, yang hidup sekitar 15 juta tahun lalu di wilayah yang kini Argentina dan merupakan burung teror terbesar yang dikenal. Pada 2007, Bertelli, Chiappe, dan Tambussi menamai spesimennya Kelenken guillermoi, dengan nama genus yang merujuk pada roh dalam mitologi Tehuelche yang digambarkan sebagai burung pemangsa raksasa.
long_description.en:
Kelenken is a demon in the mythology of the Tehuelche, the indigenous people of Patagonia (Patagonië). He is seen as a bringer of pain and disease and is depicted as a giant bird of prey.

According to the Tehuelche, night (Tons) is the legendary mother of evil spirits. When the sun and moon came together, night swiftly covered the earth, and when they parted it left the earth again. From this came three brothers: Axshem, bringer of pain; Maip, bearer of fear and misfortune; and Kelenken.

The name Kelenken was given to a genus of extinct terror bird (phorusrhacid) from Patagonia, which lived some 15 million years ago in today's Argentina and is the largest known terror bird. In 2007 Bertelli, Chiappe and Tambussi named the specimen Kelenken guillermoi, the genus name referring to a spirit of Tehuelche mythology represented as a giant bird of prey.

short_description.id: Kludde adalah setan pengubah wujud dalam cerita rakyat Flandria dan Belanda selatan, yang dengan rantai berdenting melompat ke tengkuk pejalan malam dan harus digendong hingga fajar.
short_description.en: The Kludde is a shapeshifting demon of Flemish and southern Dutch folklore who, with a rattling chain, leaps onto night walkers' necks and must be carried until dawn.

long_description.id:
Kludde adalah makhluk pengubah wujud dalam kepercayaan Jermanik dan Flandria, dikenal di Belanda serta Flandria Belgia dan Prancis. Rupanya berbeda dari cerita ke cerita: anjing hitam mengerikan yang berjalan dengan kaki belakang, kucing hitam besar, burung hitam raksasa, atau kuda; ia dapat membesar dan mengecil, dan makin cepat pejalan lari, makin cepat ia mengejar. Dalam cerita lain ia lelaki berbalut kulit anjing berbulu, mengingatkan pada manusia serigala.

Kludde adalah roh pengganggu yang bersembunyi di bawah jembatan atau di pohon berongga dan hanya keluar pada malam hari. Pejalan tahu ia datang dari bunyi rantai yang wajib dipakainya di pergelangan kaki kiri. Ia lalu melompat ke tengkuk orang yang lengah, yang harus menggendongnya sepanjang malam sampai fajar atau sampai tiba di tujuan. Dalam wujud kuda ia memperdaya para pengurus kandang dan melempar mereka ke parit.

Kludde dianggap tak terkalahkan, tetapi beberapa kisah menceritakan kekalahannya: di Schelle seorang tukang daging menikam perutnya hingga ia lari dan tak kembali, dan cerita lain menyebut doa sebagai cara meloloskan diri. Ia dikaitkan dengan daerah Schelde, Dendermonde, sekitar Antwerpen, serta Brabant Flandria; di Aalst ia disebut Kledden.
long_description.en:
The Kludde is a shapeshifter of Germanic and Flemish belief, known in the Netherlands and in Belgian and French Flanders. Its looks vary from tale to tale: a monstrous black dog walking on its hind legs, a big black cat, a giant black bird or a horse; it can grow and shrink, and the faster passers-by run, the faster it follows. In other tales it is a man wrapped in a shaggy dog skin, recalling the werewolf.

The Kludde is a tormenting spirit that hides under bridges or in hollow trees and comes out only at night. Walkers know it is coming from the sound of the chain it must wear on its left ankle. It then leaps onto an unsuspecting walker's neck, and the victim must carry it all night until daybreak or until reaching home. In horse form it tricks stable boys and throws them into a ditch.

The Kludde was thought unbeatable, yet a few tales tell of its defeat: in Schelle a butcher stabbed it in the belly so that it fled and never returned, and other stories name prayer as a way to escape. It is associated with the Scheldt region, Dendermonde, the Antwerp area and Flemish Brabant; in Aalst it was called Kledden.

short_description.id: Kornmann adalah roh ladang gandum (Korndämon) dan sosok penakut anak (Kinderschreck) lelaki dalam legenda Jerman, yang berdiam di ladang dan sawah.
short_description.en: The Kornmann is a male corn spirit (Korndämon) and child-scaring figure (Kinderschreck) of German legend who dwells in fields and farmland.

long_description.id:
Kornmann adalah roh ladang gandum (Korndämon) dan sosok penakut anak (Kinderschreck) lelaki dalam legenda Jerman, yang berdiam di ladang. Ia punya banyak nama: sebagian terkait tanaman, seperti Hafermann, Roggenmann, atau Kornvater; sebagian terkait panen, seperti Feldmann dan Erntemann; dan bentuk kecil seperti Kornmännchen yang menunjukkan wujudnya yang kadang mirip kurcaci. Korndämon adalah istilah kumpulan yang diperkenalkan Wilhelm Mannhardt untuk makhluk gaib di ladang gandum dan tanaman lain.

Kornmann memakai topi hitam besar dan tongkat yang sangat besar, bermata merah dan bermulut berapi; wajahnya hitam sehingga ia juga disebut lelaki hitam. Sebagai kurcaci ia berupa lelaki kecil hitam atau kelabu bertopi merah kecil, dan nyanyiannya adalah derik jangkrik. Ia tinggal di gua bawah tanah, mengitari tumpukan gandum, menggoda pengembara, dan membawa orang yang ditemuinya terbang di udara seperti pemburu liar.

Sebagai penakut anak, Kornmann menangkap anak-anak, memasukkan mereka ke karungnya, dan membawa mereka ke guanya, kadang hanya setahun, lebih sering selamanya. Di beberapa tempat ia mengambil alih peran Roggenmuhme atau Kornhexe yang kejam: memenggal, mencekik, atau membutakan anak, dan muncul membawa sabit sehingga disebut Sichelmann atau Sensenmann. Kadang ia juga berwujud Irrlicht atau bertindak sebagai Aufhocker. Menurut artikel tentang Korndämon, makhluk semacam ini berfungsi sebagai sosok menakutkan agar anak-anak tidak masuk dan merusak ladang yang sedang matang.
long_description.en:
The Kornmann is a male corn spirit (Korndämon) and child-scaring figure (Kinderschreck) of German legend who stays in the fields. He has many names: some tied to crops, such as Hafermann, Roggenmann or Kornvater; some to the harvest, such as Feldmann and Erntemann; and diminutives such as Kornmännchen pointing to his sometimes dwarf-like shape. Korndämon is a collective term introduced by Wilhelm Mannhardt for supernatural beings of cornfields and other crops.

The Kornmann wears a big black hat and a huge stick, has red eyes and a fiery mouth; his face is black, so he is also called the black man. As a dwarf he is a little black or grey man with a small red cap, and his song is the chirping of crickets. He lives in an underground cave, circles the corn stacks, teases wanderers and carries those he meets away through the air like the wild hunter.

As a child-scarer the Kornmann catches children, puts them in his sack and takes them to his cave, sometimes for a year, more often forever. In some places he takes over the cruel role of the Roggenmuhme or Kornhexe: beheading, strangling or blinding children, and appearing with sickles so that he is called Sichelmann or Sensenmann. He may also take the form of an Irrlicht or act as an Aufhocker. According to the article on Korndämon, such beings served as frightening figures to keep children from entering and damaging ripening fields.

short_description.id: Kornmann adalah roh ladang gandum (Korndämon) dan sosok penakut anak (Kinderschreck) lelaki dalam legenda Jerman, yang berdiam di ladang dan sawah.
short_description.en: The Kornmann is a male corn spirit (Korndämon) and child-scaring figure (Kinderschreck) of German legend who dwells in fields and farmland.

long_description.id: Kornmann adalah roh ladang gandum (Korndämon) dan sosok penakut anak (Kinderschreck) lelaki dalam legenda Jerman, yang berdiam di ladang. Ia punya banyak nama: sebagian terkait tanaman, seperti Hafermann, Roggenmann, atau Kornvater; sebagian terkait panen, seperti Feldmann dan Erntemann; dan bentuk kecil seperti Kornmännchen yang menunjukkan wujudnya yang kadang mirip kurcaci. Korndämon adalah istilah kumpulan yang diperkenalkan Wilhelm Mannhardt untuk makhluk gaib di ladang gandum dan tanaman lain.
long_description.en: The Kornmann is a male corn spirit (Korndämon) and child-scaring figure (Kinderschreck) of German legend who stays in the fields. He has many names: some tied to crops, such as Hafermann, Roggenmann or Kornvater; some to the harvest, such as Feldmann and Erntemann; and diminutives such as Kornmännchen pointing to his sometimes dwarf-like shape. Korndämon is a collective term introduced by Wilhelm Mannhardt for supernatural beings of cornfields and other crops.

long_description.id: Kornmann memakai topi hitam besar dan tongkat yang sangat besar, bermata merah dan bermulut berapi; wajahnya hitam sehingga ia juga disebut lelaki hitam. Sebagai kurcaci ia berupa lelaki kecil hitam atau kelabu bertopi merah kecil, dan nyanyiannya adalah derik jangkrik. Ia tinggal di gua bawah tanah, mengitari tumpukan gandum, menggoda pengembara, dan membawa orang yang ditemuinya terbang di udara seperti pemburu liar.
long_description.en: The Kornmann wears a big black hat and a huge stick, has red eyes and a fiery mouth; his face is black, so he is also called the black man. As a dwarf he is a little black or grey man with a small red cap, and his song is the chirping of crickets. He lives in an underground cave, circles the corn stacks, teases wanderers and carries those he meets away through the air like the wild hunter.

long_description.id: Sebagai penakut anak, Kornmann menangkap anak-anak, memasukkan mereka ke karungnya, dan membawa mereka ke guanya, kadang hanya setahun, lebih sering selamanya. Di beberapa tempat ia mengambil alih peran Roggenmuhme atau Kornhexe yang kejam: memenggal, mencekik, atau membutakan anak, dan muncul membawa sabit sehingga disebut Sichelmann atau Sensenmann. Kadang ia juga berwujud Irrlicht atau bertindak sebagai Aufhocker. Menurut artikel tentang Korndämon, makhluk semacam ini berfungsi sebagai sosok menakutkan agar anak-anak tidak masuk dan merusak ladang yang sedang matang.

In some places he takes over the cruel role of the Roggenmuhme or Kornhexe: beheading, strangling or blinding children, and appearing with sickles so that he is called Sichelmann or Sensenmann. He may also take the form of an Irrlicht or act as an Aufhocker. According to the article on Korndämon, such beings served as frightening figures to keep children from entering and damaging ripening fields.

short_description.id: Šarac adalah kuda belang bersayap milik Pangeran Marko dalam epik Serbia dan cerita rakyat Slavia Selatan, yang bisa berbicara dan minum anggur.
short_description.en: Šarac is the winged piebald horse of Prince Marko in Serbian epic and South Slavic folklore, able to speak and drink wine.

long_description.id:
Šarac adalah kuda Pangeran Marko, pahlawan puisi epik Serbia dan cerita rakyat Slavia Selatan. Ia kuda belang yang warnanya mirip sapi, bersayap, dan secepat peri. Ia memahami dan berbicara bahasa Serbia, Turki, dan Yunani, minum anggur bersama tuannya, menasihatinya, menolongnya di medan perang, dan merasakan firasat kematiannya.

Marko mendapatkannya dari samovila atau membelinya sebagai anak kuda bungkuk yang tak bergeser saat ekornya ditarik, lalu menyembuhkannya dan mengajarinya minum anggur. Menurut tradisi lisan, Marko sendiri membunuh Šarac agar tidak dipakai orang Turki untuk kerja kasar.
long_description.en:
Šarac is the horse of Prince Marko, hero of Serbian epic poetry and South Slavic folklore. He is a piebald horse coloured like a cow, winged and as fast as a fairy. He understands and speaks Serbian, Turkish and Greek, drinks wine with his master, advises him, helps him in battle and foresees his death.

Marko got him from the samovilas, or bought him as a hunchbacked foal that would not budge when he pulled its tail, then healed it and taught it to drink wine. Oral tradition says Marko himself killed Šarac so the Turks would not use him for menial work.

short_description.id: Šarac adalah kuda belang bersayap milik Pangeran Marko dalam epik Serbia dan cerita rakyat Slavia Selatan, yang bisa berbicara dan minum anggur.
short_description.en: Šarac is the winged piebald horse of Prince Marko in Serbian epic and South Slavic folklore, able to speak and drink wine.

long_description.id: Šarac adalah kuda Pangeran Marko, pahlawan puisi epik Serbia dan cerita rakyat Slavia Selatan. Ia kuda belang yang warnanya mirip sapi, bersayap, dan secepat peri. Ia memahami dan berbicara bahasa Serbia, Turki, dan Yunani, minum anggur bersama tuannya, menasihatinya, menolongnya di medan perang, dan merasakan firasat kematiannya.
long_description.en: Šarac is the horse of Prince Marko, hero of Serbian epic poetry and South Slavic folklore. He is a piebald horse coloured like a cow, winged and as fast as a fairy. He understands and speaks Serbian, Turkish and Greek, drinks wine with his master, advises him, helps him in battle and foresees his death.

long_description.id: Marko mendapatkannya dari samovila atau membelinya sebagai anak kuda bungkuk yang tak bergeser saat ekornya ditarik, lalu menyembuhkannya dan mengajarinya minum anggur. Menurut tradisi lisan, Marko sendiri membunuh Šarac agar tidak dipakai orang Turki untuk kerja kasar.
long_description.en: Marko got him from the samovilas, or bought him as a hunchbacked foal that would not budge when he pulled its tail, then healed it and taught it to drink wine. Oral tradition says Marko himself killed Šarac so the Turks would not use him for menial work.

short_description.id: Daksha adalah dewa Hindu yang dalam Rigveda merupakan Aditya terkait keterampilan kependetaan.
short_description.en: Daksha is a Hindu deity who in the Rigveda is an Aditya associated with priestly skills.

long_description.id:
Daksha adalah dewa Hindu yang dalam Rigveda merupakan Aditya terkait keterampilan kependetaan. Dalam wiracarita dan Purana ia adalah putra Brahma dan salah satu Prajapati, agen penciptaan.

Kisahnya menyebut pengorbanan yang sengaja tidak mengundang Sati dan Shiva. Dalam versi Linga Purana, Virabhadra memenggalnya dan ia kemudian hidup kembali berkepala kambing. Ikonografinya berupa laki-laki bertubuh kekar dengan wajah manusia atau kepala kambing. Dalam retelling Mackenzie, Shiva sendiri memenggal Daksha dan mengganti kepalanya dengan kepala kambing.
long_description.en:
Daksha is a Hindu deity who in the Rigveda is an Aditya associated with priestly skills. In epics and Puranas he is Brahma's son and one of the Prajapatis, agents of creation.

His narrative describes a sacrifice deliberately excluding Sati and Shiva. In the Linga Purana version Virabhadra beheads him and he later revives with a goat's head. His iconography is a stocky man with a human face or goat's head. In Mackenzie's retelling Shiva himself beheads Daksha and replaces his head with a goat's head.

short_description.id: Nekhbet adalah dewi Mesir pelindung Nekheb yang kemudian melindungi Mesir Hulu.
short_description.en: Nekhbet is an Egyptian goddess protecting Nekheb and later Upper Egypt.

long_description.id:
Nekhbet adalah dewi Mesir pelindung Nekheb yang kemudian melindungi Mesir Hulu. Kuil awalnya berada di Nekheb atau El Kab.

Ia dan Wadjet tampil sebagai Dua Nyonya dalam gelar kerajaan. Ia digambarkan sebagai burung nasar. Ia melayang dengan sayap terentang dan simbol shen sebagai perlindungan kekal. Sumber pendamping menegaskan pasangan Nekhbet dan Wadjet sebagai Dua Nyonya.
long_description.en:
Nekhbet is an Egyptian goddess protecting Nekheb and later Upper Egypt. Her early shrine is at Nekheb or El Kab.

She and Wadjet appear as the Two Ladies in royal titles. She is depicted as a vulture. She hovers with spread wings and a shen symbol for eternal protection. The accompanying source confirms Nekhbet and Wadjet as the Two Ladies.

long_description.id:
Tefnut adalah dewi kelembapan Mesir dan anggota Ennead Heliopolis. Atum disebut sebagai orang tuanya. Shu adalah saudara laki-laki sekaligus pasangannya.

Geb dan Nut adalah anak-anaknya bersama Shu. Ia berupa singa betina atau dewi berkepala singa. Ia membantu Shu menopang langit dan menjaga kestabilan dunia. Dalam satu kisah ia pergi dari Mesir ke gurun Nubia sebagai singa betina ganas. Ia dapat diidentifikasi dengan Bastet, Sekhmet, dan Hathor.

Sumber ini menggambarkan Tefnut sebagai dewi atmosfer dekat bumi. Namanya dikaitkan dengan bunyi meludah dalam penafsiran yang dikutip sumber. Seni juga menggambarkannya sebagai ular berkepala singa. Satu versi penciptaan melahirkan Shu dan Tefnut lewat ludah Atum. Budge menghubungkan Tefnut sebagai dewi orang mati dengan minuman bagi almarhum. Dalam uraian Budge, Tefnut adalah mata kiri Temu, dibandingkan dengan bulan. Temu, Shu, dan Tefnut membentuk tiga serangkai dalam teks penciptaan yang dikutip Budge.
long_description.en:
Tefnut is an Egyptian moisture goddess belonging to the Heliopolitan Ennead. Atum is named as her parent. Shu is her brother and consort.

Geb and Nut are her children with Shu. She takes the form of a lioness or lion-headed goddess. She helps Shu support the sky and maintain the world’s stability. In one tale she leaves Egypt for the Nubian desert as a fierce lioness. She can be identified with Bastet, Sekhmet and Hathor.

This source describes Tefnut as goddess of the atmosphere near the earth. Her name is associated with the sound of spitting in the interpretation cited by this source. Art also depicts her as a lion-headed serpent. One creation version produces Shu and Tefnut through Atum’s spitting. Budge connects Tefnut as a goddess of the dead with drink for the deceased. In Budge’s account Tefnut is Temu’s left eye, compared with the moon. Temu, Shu and Tefnut form a trinity in the creation text cited by Budge.

short_description.id: Əməgen adalah raksasa buruk rupa, kadang berkepala banyak, dalam legenda Turk, Altai, Kaukasus, dan Nart; menurut epos Nart, ia sumber segala kejahatan di dunia.
short_description.en: The Əməgen is an ugly, sometimes many-headed giant of Turkic, Altaic, Caucasian and Nart legends; in the Nart epics it is the source of all evil in the world.

long_description.id:
Əməgen, yang juga disebut İmegen, adalah raksasa dalam legenda Turk, Altai, Kaukasus, dan Nart. Ia digambarkan sebagai makhluk raksasa yang buruk rupa dan kadang memiliki lebih dari satu kepala. Dalam legenda Kaukasus, gambaran yang sama dicatat: makhluk raksasa yang jelek dan kadang berkepala banyak.

Dalam legenda Nart, jumlah Əməgen sangat banyak; mereka disebut melahirkan setiap tiga bulan dan tiap kelahiran menghasilkan banyak anak, bahkan menurut kamus legenda Turk lebih dari seratus. Mereka memangsa manusia yang tertangkap, sehingga para pahlawan Nart, walau selalu menang berkat kekuatan dan kecerdikan, tetap sangat takut kepada mereka.

Menurut epos Nart, Əməgen adalah sumber semua kejahatan di dunia. Para dewa menciptakan kaum Nart untuk melindungi bumi dari kejahatan mereka, dan tidak ada satu pun kisah Nart yang tidak menampilkan Əməgen.
long_description.en:
The Əməgen, also called İmegen, is a giant in Turkic, Altaic, Caucasian and Nart legends. It is described as a huge, ugly being that sometimes has more than one head. Caucasian legends record the same picture: a gigantic, ugly and sometimes many-headed creature.

In the Nart legends the Əməgens are very numerous; they are said to give birth every three months, with many children at each birth, more than a hundred according to a Turkic legend dictionary. They devour any people they catch, so the Nart heroes, though they always win through strength and wit, still greatly fear them.

According to the Nart epics, the Əməgens are the source of all evil in the world. The gods created the Narts to protect the earth from their wickedness, and there is no Nart tale in which the Əməgens do not appear.

literal_meaning.id: dari akar Em/Əm; kata emen berarti ruh, jiwa; menurut kamus legenda Turk, nama ini berarti raksasa perempuan
literal_meaning.en: from the root Em/Əm; the word emen means spirit, soul; according to a Turkic legend dictionary the name means female giant

summary.en: Türk Söylence Sözlüğü says the name means female giant and that they are in fact female beings.

claim.en: They are described as ugly (çirkin) giant beings (nəhəng varlıqlar), at times with more than one head (başı).

claims_provenance.quote: Çirkin, zaman-zaman birdən çox başı olan nəhəng varlıqlar olaraq təsvir edilər.

claim.id: Dalam legenda Nart jumlah mereka sangat banyak; mereka disebut berbiak setiap tiga (üç) bulan dan melahirkan banyak anak setiap kali.
claim.en: In Nart legends (Nart əfsanələrində) they are very numerous, said to breed every three (üç) months and to bear many children (çox uşaq) at each birth.

claims_provenance.quote: Nart əfsanələrində ədədləri olduqca çoxdur və hər üç ayda bir ad etdikləri deyilər. Hər doğumda görə çox uşaq dünyaya gətirirlər.

claim.id: Para pahlawan Nart terus berperang melawan emegen dan selalu menang dengan kekuatan dan kecerdikan, tetapi tetap sangat takut kepada mereka.
claim.en: The Nart heroes (Nart qəhrəmanları) fight the emegens continually and always defeat them by strength and wit, yet greatly fear them.

claims_provenance.quote: Nart qəhrəmanları davamlı emegenlerle vuruşub və gücləriylə, zəkalarıyla onları hər vaxt yenmeyi bacararlar. Lakin onlardan çox qorxar və çəkinirlər.

short_description.id: Əməgen adalah raksasa buruk rupa, kadang berkepala banyak, dalam legenda Turk, Altai, Kaukasus, dan Nart; menurut epos Nart, ia sumber segala kejahatan di dunia.
short_description.en: The Əməgen is an ugly, sometimes many-headed giant of Turkic, Altaic, Caucasian and Nart legends; in the Nart epics it is the source of all evil in the world.

long_description.id: Əməgen, yang juga disebut İmegen, adalah raksasa dalam legenda Turk, Altai, Kaukasus, dan Nart. Ia digambarkan sebagai makhluk raksasa yang buruk rupa dan kadang memiliki lebih dari satu kepala. Dalam legenda Kaukasus, gambaran yang sama dicatat: makhluk raksasa yang jelek dan kadang berkepala banyak.
long_description.en: The Əməgen, also called İmegen, is a giant in Turkic, Altaic, Caucasian and Nart legends. It is described as a huge, ugly being that sometimes has more than one head. Caucasian legends record the same picture: a gigantic, ugly and sometimes many-headed creature.

long_description.id: Dalam legenda Nart, jumlah Əməgen sangat banyak; mereka disebut melahirkan setiap tiga bulan dan tiap kelahiran menghasilkan banyak anak, bahkan menurut kamus legenda Turk lebih dari seratus. Mereka memangsa manusia yang tertangkap, sehingga para pahlawan Nart, walau selalu menang berkat kekuatan dan kecerdikan, tetap sangat takut kepada mereka.
long_description.en: In the Nart legends the Əməgens are very numerous; they are said to give birth every three months, with many children at each birth, more than a hundred according to a Turkic legend dictionary. They devour any people they catch, so the Nart heroes, though they always win through strength and wit, still greatly fear them.

long_description.id: Menurut epos Nart, Əməgen adalah sumber semua kejahatan di dunia. Para dewa menciptakan kaum Nart untuk melindungi bumi dari kejahatan mereka, dan tidak ada satu pun kisah Nart yang tidak menampilkan Əməgen.
long_description.en: According to the Nart epics, the Əməgens are the source of all evil in the world. The gods created the Narts to protect the earth from their wickedness, and there is no Nart tale in which the Əməgens do not appear.

short_description.id: Mo-o (juga mo-ko) adalah hewan dongeng, naga laut besar dari Polinesia; di Hawaii, moʻo adalah roh kadal yang dapat berganti wujud.
short_description.en: The mo-o (also mo-ko) is a fabulous beast, the great sea dragon of Polynesia; in Hawaii the moʻo are shapeshifting lizard spirits.

long_description.id:
Mo-o (juga disebut mo-ko) adalah hewan dongeng (fabeldier), naga laut besar dari Polinesia (Polynesië). Dahulu di Polinesia berbagai fauna disebut Mo-O: buaya, aligator, belut, penyu laut besar, ikan besar, hiu, dan sebagainya. Seekor mo-o bernama Kane-kua-ana konon hidup di Ewabaai (kini Pearl Harbor); menurut penduduk setempat, sekitar 1850 naga itu memindahkan hamparan tiram dari pantai mereka ke bagian laut lain karena marah kepada para pencari tiram, kesimpulan yang mereka tarik ketika tangkapan tiram mulai berkurang.

Dalam mitologi Hawaii, moʻo adalah roh kadal yang dapat berganti wujud, sering mengambil wujud reptil raksasa, tokek kecil, atau manusia. Mereka dihormati sebagai ʻaumakua (leluhur pelindung), dapat menguasai cuaca dan air, bersifat amfibi, dan banyak kolam ikan di Hawaii dipercaya menjadi rumah seekor moʻo. Bila moʻo mati, tubuhnya yang membatu menjadi bagian dari bentang alam. Dalam kisah Hiʻiaka, dewi itu membunuh moʻo pemakan manusia Kikipua, yang lidahnya menyamar sebagai jembatan papan di atas jurang di Molokaʻi.
long_description.en:
The mo-o (also called mo-ko) is a fabulous beast (fabeldier), the great sea dragon of Polynesia (Polynesië). In Polynesia a wide range of fauna was once called Mo-O: crocodiles, alligators, eels, large sea turtles, big fish, sharks and so on. A mo-o named Kane-kua-ana was said to live in the Ewabaai (now Pearl Harbor); according to the locals, around 1850 this dragon moved an oyster bed from their coast to another part of the ocean because it was angry with the oyster fishers, a conclusion they drew when the oyster catch began to decline.

In Hawaiian mythology the moʻo are shapeshifting lizard spirits, often taking the form of monstrous reptiles, tiny geckos or humans. They were revered as ʻaumakua (ancestral guardians), could have power over weather and water, lived both in water and on land, and many Hawaiian fishponds were thought to shelter one. A dead moʻo turns to stone and becomes a feature of the land. In the tale of Hiʻiaka, the goddess kills the man-eating moʻo Kikipua, whose tongue posed as a plank bridge across a ravine on Molokaʻi.

statement.id: Mo-o (juga mo-ko) adalah hewan dongeng (fabeldier), naga laut besar (grote zeedraak) dari Polinesia (Polynesië).
statement.en: The mo-o (also mo-ko) is a fabulous beast (fabeldier), the great sea dragon (grote zeedraak) of Polynesia (Polynesië).

claims.quote: In Polynesia werd vroeger een brede verzameling fauna betiteld als Mo-O; krokodillen, alligators, alen, grote zeeschildpadden, grote vissen, haaien enzovoorts.

statement.id: Di Polinesia (Polynesia) berbagai fauna disebut Mo-O: buaya (krokodillen), aligator, belut (alen), penyu laut (zeeschildpadden), ikan besar (vissen), hiu (haaien).
statement.en: In Polynesia many fauna were called Mo-O: crocodiles (krokodillen), alligators, eels (alen), sea turtles (zeeschildpadden), big fish (vissen), sharks (haaien).

claims.quote: Een mo-o met de naam Kane-kua-ana zou geleefd hebben in de Ewabaai (nu Pearl Harbor). Volgens de plaatselijke bevolking zou deze draak rond 1850 een oesterbed van hun kust naar een ander stuk van de oceaan hebben verplaatst, omdat hij boos was geworden op de oestervissers.

statement.id: Mo-o bernama Kane-kua-ana hidup di Ewabaai (kini Pearl Harbor); sekitar 1850 naga (draak) itu memindahkan hamparan tiram (oesterbed) karena marah (boos) kepada pencari tiram (oestervissers).
statement.en: A mo-o named Kane-kua-ana lived in Ewabaai (now Pearl Harbor); around 1850 the dragon (draak) moved an oyster bed (oesterbed) because it was angry (boos) with the oyster fishers (oestervissers).

claims.quote: Moʻo are shapeshifting lizard spirits in Hawaiian mythology.

statement.en: Moʻo are shapeshifting lizard spirits in Hawaiian mythology.

claims.quote: Moʻo often take the forms of monstrous reptiles, tiny geckos, and/or humans. They were revered as ʻaumakua, and could have power over the weather and water. They were amphibious, and many fishponds in Hawaii were believed to be home to a moʻo.

statement.id: Moʻo berwujud reptil raksasa, tokek kecil, atau manusia; dihormati sebagai ʻaumakua, menguasai cuaca dan air, dan kolam ikan di Hawaii dipercaya rumah moʻo.
statement.en: Moʻo take the forms of monstrous reptiles, tiny geckos or humans; revered as ʻaumakua, with power over weather and water; many fishponds in Hawaii were home to a moʻo.

claims.quote: When a moʻo dies, its petrified body becomes part of the landscape.

statement.id: Bila moʻo mati, tubuhnya yang membatu (petrified) menjadi bagian bentang alam (landscape).
statement.en: When a moʻo dies, its petrified body becomes part of the landscape.

statement.en: Hiʻiaka recognizes the bewitched bridge as the tongue of the man-eating moʻo Kikipua, chases it and kills it; Wahineʻomaʻo had started across.

claims.quote: On the windward cliffs of Molokaʻi, the young goddess and her attendant Wahineʻomaʻo come to an impassable ravine.

short_description.id: Ochokochi ("manusia-kambing") adalah makhluk setengah manusia setengah kambing dalam mitologi Georgia, khususnya Mingrelia, yang menyerang orang di hutan dan mengejar ratu hutan Tkashi-Mapa.
short_description.en: Ochokochi ("goat-man") is a half-man, half-goat being of Georgian, especially Mingrelian, mythology who attacks people in the forest and chases the forest queen Tkashi-Mapa.

long_description.id:
Ochokochi, harfiah "manusia-kambing", adalah tokoh mitologi Georgia, terutama kelompok Kolkhis dan Mingrelia: makhluk setengah manusia setengah kambing, dewa hutan jahat yang selalu berkonflik dengan pemburu dan pengumpul. Ia digambarkan raksasa berbulu merah karat dengan cakar panjang tajam, dan alih-alih bulu di dada ia memiliki tonjolan berbentuk tulang runcing atau kapak batu, yang dipakainya membelah lawan menjadi dua. Ia menyerang orang yang lewat dan membunuh mereka dengan memeluknya.

Ia tidak dapat berbicara, tetapi suaranya yang bergemuruh membuat orang sangat ketakutan, dan ia paling dekat dengan Pan dalam mitos Yunani. Ia tergila-gila pada kecantikan ratu hutan Tkashi-Mapa dan terus mengejarnya, tetapi usahanya sering digagalkan para pemburu. Ochokochi yang dibunuh pemburu dapat hidup kembali setelah ditembak atau ditebas sekali lagi, dan sampai kini ia tokoh cerita seram untuk menakuti anak-anak nakal di Georgia Barat.
long_description.en:
Ochokochi, literally "goat-man", is a figure of Georgian, especially Colchian and Mingrelian, mythology: a half-man, half-goat evil forest deity in constant conflict with hunters and gatherers. He is pictured as a huge monster with rust-red fur and long sharp claws, and instead of hair on his breast he has a pointed bone or stone-axe protrusion used to cleave enemies in two. He attacks passers-by and kills them by embracing them.

He cannot speak, but his rumbling voice fills people with indescribable fear, and he is closest to Pan of Greek myth. He is infatuated with the beauty of the forest queen Tkashi-Mapa and pursues her, though hunters often foil him. An Ochokochi killed by hunters could revive after a second shot or sword blow, and he remains a bogey used to scare naughty children in western Georgia.

short_description.id: Perun adalah dewa tertinggi dalam mitologi Slavia, penguasa langit, guruh, dan petir, yang juga dikaitkan dengan perang, hukum, dan pohon ek.
short_description.en: Perun is the highest god of Slavic mythology, lord of the sky, thunder and lightning, also linked with war, law and oak trees.

long_description.id:
Dalam mitologi Slavia, Perun menempati puncak jajaran dewa. Ia memerintah langit, guruh, petir, badai, dan hujan, serta berkaitan dengan hukum, perang, kesuburan, dan pohon ek. Lambang lain yang melekat padanya antara lain api, gunung, angin, bunga iris, elang, kuda dan kereta, serta senjata berupa palu, kapak, dan anak panah. Para peneliti juga menggambarkannya sebagai dewa badai tertinggi yang dihubungkan dengan batu, guruh, kilat, hujan, perang, dan keadilan.

Di Rus Kiev pada abad ke-9 sampai ke-10 ia adalah dewa tertinggi, mula-mula dikaitkan dengan senjata batu lalu dengan senjata logam. Ia sudah disebut pada abad ke-6 oleh sejarawan Romawi Timur Procopius dalam De Bello Gothico. Pada tahun 980 Vladimir mendirikan arca lima dewa pagan di depan istananya, dan Perun menjadi yang utama, dengan kepala perak dan kumis emas. Hari rayanya dirayakan dengan persembahan pada bulan Juli.

Menurut kepercayaan rakyat, kilat Perun berupa batu dan anak panah batu, sehingga fulgurit, belemnit, dan perkakas batu prasejarah yang ditemukan di tanah dianggap sisa senjatanya. Senjata itu dipercaya melindungi dari nasib buruk, sihir jahat, penyakit, dan petir. Satu sumber menggambarkannya sebagai lelaki paruh baya berjanggut yang terbang di atas batu gilingan sambil melepaskan kilat dan guruh.

Perun dikatakan menikahi Matahari, tetapi berbagi istri dengan musuhnya Veles, karena Matahari setiap malam turun ke dunia bawah yang dikuasai Veles. Tempat pemujaannya berada di puncak gunung atau bukit, atau di hutan keramat di bawah pohon ek tua, dengan persembahan banteng, sapi, domba jantan, dan telur. Ia juga dihubungkan dengan hari Kamis dan dengan logam timah.

Setelah masuk Kristen, Vladimir memerintahkan arca-arca Perun dirobohkan, diseret, dipukuli, lalu dibuang ke sungai; menurut satu sumber arcanya dilempar ke Sungai Dnipro dan di tempatnya dibangun Gereja Santo Basil. Gereja menggantikan pemujaan Perun dengan pemujaan Santo Elia, yang mewarisi semua sifat Perun, tetapi orang Lemko masih menganggap ungkapan "Semoga Perun menyambarmu mati" sebagai kutukan paling mengerikan. Kini Perun termasuk dewa yang paling dihormati dalam neopaganisme Slavia (rodnovery), sebagai dewa pejuang dan saingan Veles.
long_description.en:
In Slavic mythology Perun stands at the top of the pantheon. He rules the sky, thunder, lightning, storms and rain, and is tied to law, war, fertility and oak trees. Other emblems attached to him include fire, mountains, wind, the iris, the eagle, horses and carts, and weapons such as the hammer, the axe and the arrow. Scholars also describe him as a supreme storm god connected with rock, thunder, lightning, rain, war and justice.

In Kievan Rus during the 9th and 10th centuries he was the supreme god, associated first with stone weapons and later with metal ones. He was already mentioned in the 6th century by the Eastern Roman historian Procopius in De Bello Gothico. In 980 Vladimir set up statues of five pagan gods before his palace, with Perun foremost among them, bearing a silver head and a golden moustache. His feast was celebrated with sacrifices in July.

In folk belief Perun's lightning bolts were stones and stone arrows, so fulgurites, belemnites and prehistoric stone tools found in the ground were taken as remains of his weapons. These weapons were thought to guard against bad luck, evil magic, disease and lightning. One source pictures him as a bearded middle-aged man flying on a millstone while hurling lightning and thunder.

Perun was said to be married to the Sun, but he shared his wife with his enemy Veles, since the Sun sank each night into the underworld ruled by Veles. His shrines stood on mountain tops or hills, or in sacred groves under ancient oaks, with offerings of a bull, an ox, a ram and eggs. He was also linked with Thursday and with tin.

After his conversion Vladimir had the statues of Perun torn down, dragged, beaten and thrown into rivers; one source says the statue was cast into the Dnipro River and Saint Basil's Church was built on its site. The Church replaced the cult of Perun with that of Saint Elijah, who inherited all his qualities, yet the Lemkos still regard "May Perun strike you dead" as the most terrible curse. Today Perun is among the most revered gods of Slavic neopaganism (rodnovery), as a god of warriors and a rival of Veles.

claim.en: To this day, in a number of Slavic languages the word perun means "thunder" or "lightning bolt".

claims_provenance.quote: To this day, the word perun in a number of Slavic languages means "thunder," or "lightning bolt".

claim.id: Sejak abad ke-6 ia sudah disebut dalam De Bello Gothico, sumber sejarah karya sejarawan Romawi Timur Procopius.
claim.en: As early as the 6th century he was mentioned in De Bello Gothico, a historical source by the Eastern Roman historian Procopius.

claims_provenance.quote: As early as the 6th century, he was mentioned in De Bello Gothico, a historical source written by the Eastern Roman historian Procopius.

claim.id: Pada tahun 980, ketika pangeran Vladimir Agung naik takhta di Kiev, ia mendirikan arca lima dewa pagan di depan istananya, yang kemudian ia singkirkan setelah masuk Kristen pada 988; Perun adalah yang utama, digambarkan berkepala perak dan berkumis emas.
claim.en: In 980, when Prince Vladimir the Great took the throne of Kiev, he erected statues of five pagan gods before his palace, discarding them after his Christianization in 988; Perun was chief among them, with a silver head and a golden moustache.

claims_provenance.quote: In 980, when prince Vladimir the Great came to the throne of Kiev, he erected statues of five pagan gods in front of his palace which he soon thereafter discarded after his Christianization in 988. Perun was chief among these, represented with a silver head and a golden moustache.

claim.id: Perun sangat berkaitan dengan Perkūnas/Pērkons yang hampir identik dari mitologi Baltik, yang menunjukkan asal bersama dari dewa guruh Proto-Indo-Eropa atau peminjaman.
claim.en: Perun is strongly correlated with the near-identical Perkūnas/Pērkons of Baltic mythology, suggesting a common Proto-Indo-European thunder god origin or borrowing.

claims_provenance.quote: Perun is strongly correlated with the near-identical Perkūnas/Pērkons from Baltic mythology, suggesting either a common derivative of the Proto-Indo European thunder god

claim.id: Akar *perkwu semula mungkin berarti pohon ek, tetapi dalam bahasa Proto-Slavia berkembang menjadi *per- yang berarti "memukul, membunuh".
claim.en: The root *perkwu probably first meant oak, but in Proto-Slavic it became *per-, meaning "to strike, to slay".

claims_provenance.quote: The root *perkwu originally probably meant oak, but in Proto-Slavic this evolved into *per- meaning "to strike, to slay".

claim.id: Kilat Perun dipercaya berupa batu dan anak panah batu; menurut kepercayaan rakyat, fulgurit, belemnit, dan kadang perkakas batu prasejarah yang ditemukan di tanah adalah sisa senjata itu.
claim.en: Perun's lightning bolts were believed to be stones and stone arrows; folk belief held fulgurites, belemnites and sometimes prehistoric stone tools found in the ground to be remains of these weapons.

claims_provenance.quote: Perun's lightning bolts were believed to be stones and stone arrows. According to folk beliefs, fulgurites, belemnites, and sometimes even the remains of prehistoric stone tools found in the ground are remains of these weapons.

claim.id: Senjata Perun melindungi dari nasib buruk, sihir jahat, penyakit, dan juga dari petir itu sendiri.
claim.en: The weapons of Perun protected against bad luck, evil magic, disease and lightning itself.

claims_provenance.quote: The weapons of Perun protected against bad luck, evil magic, disease, and – naturally enough – lightning itself.

claim.id: Perun dapat ditunjukkan menikahi Matahari, tetapi ia berbagi istri dengan musuhnya Veles, karena setiap malam Matahari dianggap terbenam ke dunia bawah, alam orang mati yang dikuasai Veles.
claim.en: Perun can be shown to have been married to the Sun, but he shared his wife with his enemy Veles, as each night the Sun was thought to dive into the underworld, the realm of the dead ruled by Veles.

claims_provenance.quote: it can also be shown that Perun was married to the Sun. He, however, shared his wife with his enemy Veles, as each night the Sun was thought of as diving behind the horizon and into the underworld, the realm of the dead over which Veles ruled.

claim.id: Tempat pemujaan Perun berada di puncak gunung atau bukit, atau di hutan keramat di bawah pohon ek tua; di sana dilakukan ibadah dan persembahan berupa banteng, sapi, domba jantan, dan telur.
claim.en: Perun's shrines stood on mountain tops or hills, or in sacred groves under ancient oaks, as places of worship and sacrifice (a bull, an ox, a ram and eggs).

claims_provenance.quote: Shrines of Perun were located either on top of mountains or hills, or in sacred groves underneath ancient oaks. These were general places of worship and sacrifices (with a bull, an ox, a ram, and eggs).

claim.id: Selain pohon, Perun juga dikaitkan dengan satu hari, yaitu Kamis (Thursday), dan dengan satu bahan, yaitu timah.
claim.en: Besides the tree, Perun was associated with a day (Thursday) and a material (tin).

claims_provenance.quote: In addition to the tree association, Perun had a day association (Thursday) as well as the material association (tin).

claim.id: Ia memerintahkan agar arca-arca Perun yang dulu didirikannya sendiri dirobohkan dengan hina dan diseret di jalan sambil dipukuli tongkat, lalu dibuang ke sungai dan tidak dibiarkan terdampar di tepi.
claim.en: He ordered the statues of Perun he had once erected to be torn down in disgrace and dragged through the streets while beaten with sticks, then cast into rivers and not allowed to land on the shore.

claims_provenance.quote: He ordered that the statues of Perun which he himself had erected formerly, be dethroned, torn down with great dishonor and dragged through the streets as they were beaten with sticks. The idols were then cast into rivers and not permitted to land on the shore.

claim.id: Perun adalah salah satu dewa yang paling dihormati dalam neopaganisme Slavia (rodnovery); ia dianggap dewa guruh, dewa para pejuang, dan saingan Veles, serta perwujudan badai musim semi yang menyuburkan bumi.
claim.en: Perun is one of the most revered gods of Slavic neopaganism (rodnovery), seen as a thunderer, god of warriors and rival of Veles, embodying spring storms that fertilize the earth.

claims_provenance.quote: Perun is one of the most revered gods in Slavic neopaganism (rodnovery). He is considered a thunderer, the god of warriors, and a rival of Veles, also embodying spring thunderstorms that fertilize the earth.

claim.id: Suku-suku Baltik memuja dewa guruh Perkunas, salah satu dewa utama mereka, yang memiliki atribut sama dengan Perun: jimat berbentuk kapak, simbol api berujung empat, dan pohon ek sebagai pohon utama.
claim.en: The Baltic tribes widely worshipped the thunderer Perkunas, a main Baltic deity sharing attributes with Perun: axe amulets, a fiery four-pointed symbol and the oak as chief tree.

claims_provenance.quote: The Baltic tribes had a widespread cult of the thunderer Perkunas, one of the main deities of the Baltic pantheon. With Perun, this deity also shares common attributes (amulets in the form of an axe, a fiery four-pointed symbol, oak as the main tree)

claims_provenance.quote: Among South Slavs, a mountain plant Iris germanica is known in folklore as perunika ("Perun's plant") and sometimes also as bogisha ("god's plant"), and was believed to grow from ground that had been struck by lightning.

claims_provenance.quote: Perun. One of the principal deities in eastern and northern Slavic mythology. In pre-Christian Kyivan Rus’ this was the chief god—the god of thunder, lightning, and rain, the ruler of the heavens, and, later, the god of war.

claim.en: In 980 a wooden statue of Perun with a silver head and golden moustache stood on Perun Hill in Kyiv; his feast, with sacrifices, took place in July.

claims_provenance.quote: In 980 a wooden statue of Perun with a silver head and golden moustache stood on Perun Hill in Kyiv. Perun's feast, celebrated with sacrifices, took place in July.

claim.en: For more than a century, scholars of Slavic mythology have assumed a connection between the German iris (Iris germanica) and the cult of Perun.

claims_provenance.quote: For more than a century, scholars of Slavic mythology have adopted the assumption connecting the German iris (Iris germanica) plant and the cult of the god Perun.

short_description.id: Perun adalah dewa tertinggi dalam mitologi Slavia, penguasa langit, guruh, dan petir, yang juga dikaitkan dengan perang, hukum, dan pohon ek.
short_description.en: Perun is the highest god of Slavic mythology, lord of the sky, thunder and lightning, also linked with war, law and oak trees.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi Slavia, Perun menempati puncak jajaran dewa. Ia memerintah langit, guruh, petir, badai, dan hujan, serta berkaitan dengan hukum, perang, kesuburan, dan pohon ek. Lambang lain yang melekat padanya antara lain api, gunung, angin, bunga iris, elang, kuda dan kereta, serta senjata berupa palu, kapak, dan anak panah. Para peneliti juga menggambarkannya sebagai dewa badai tertinggi yang dihubungkan dengan batu, guruh, kilat, hujan, perang, dan keadilan.
long_description.en: In Slavic mythology Perun stands at the top of the pantheon. He rules the sky, thunder, lightning, storms and rain, and is tied to law, war, fertility and oak trees. Other emblems attached to him include fire, mountains, wind, the iris, the eagle, horses and carts, and weapons such as the hammer, the axe and the arrow. Scholars also describe him as a supreme storm god connected with rock, thunder, lightning, rain, war and justice.

long_description.id: Di Rus Kiev pada abad ke-9 sampai ke-10 ia adalah dewa tertinggi, mula-mula dikaitkan dengan senjata batu lalu dengan senjata logam. Ia sudah disebut pada abad ke-6 oleh sejarawan Romawi Timur Procopius dalam De Bello Gothico. Pada tahun 980 Vladimir mendirikan arca lima dewa pagan di depan istananya, dan Perun menjadi yang utama, dengan kepala perak dan kumis emas. Hari rayanya dirayakan dengan persembahan pada bulan Juli.
long_description.en: In Kievan Rus during the 9th and 10th centuries he was the supreme god, associated first with stone weapons and later with metal ones. He was already mentioned in the 6th century by the Eastern Roman historian Procopius in De Bello Gothico. In 980 Vladimir set up statues of five pagan gods before his palace, with Perun foremost among them, bearing a silver head and a golden moustache. His feast was celebrated with sacrifices in July.

long_description.id: Menurut kepercayaan rakyat, kilat Perun berupa batu dan anak panah batu, sehingga fulgurit, belemnit, dan perkakas batu prasejarah yang ditemukan di tanah dianggap sisa senjatanya. Senjata itu dipercaya melindungi dari nasib buruk, sihir jahat, penyakit, dan petir. Satu sumber menggambarkannya sebagai lelaki paruh baya berjanggut yang terbang di atas batu gilingan sambil melepaskan kilat dan guruh.
long_description.en: In folk belief Perun's lightning bolts were stones and stone arrows, so fulgurites, belemnites and prehistoric stone tools found in the ground were taken as remains of his weapons. These weapons were thought to guard against bad luck, evil magic, disease and lightning. One source pictures him as a bearded middle-aged man flying on a millstone while hurling lightning and thunder.

long_description.id: Perun dikatakan menikahi Matahari, tetapi berbagi istri dengan musuhnya Veles, karena Matahari setiap malam turun ke dunia bawah yang dikuasai Veles. Tempat pemujaannya berada di puncak gunung atau bukit, atau di hutan keramat di bawah pohon ek tua, dengan persembahan banteng, sapi, domba jantan, dan telur. Ia juga dihubungkan dengan hari Kamis dan dengan logam timah.
long_description.en: Perun was said to be married to the Sun, but he shared his wife with his enemy Veles, since the Sun sank each night into the underworld ruled by Veles. His shrines stood on mountain tops or hills, or in sacred groves under ancient oaks, with offerings of a bull, an ox, a ram and eggs. He was also linked with Thursday and with tin.

long_description.id: Setelah masuk Kristen, Vladimir memerintahkan arca-arca Perun dirobohkan, diseret, dipukuli, lalu dibuang ke sungai; menurut satu sumber arcanya dilempar ke Sungai Dnipro dan di tempatnya dibangun Gereja Santo Basil. Gereja menggantikan pemujaan Perun dengan pemujaan Santo Elia, yang mewarisi semua sifat Perun, tetapi orang Lemko masih menganggap ungkapan "Semoga Perun menyambarmu mati" sebagai kutukan paling mengerikan. Kini Perun termasuk dewa yang paling dihormati dalam neopaganisme Slavia (rodnovery), sebagai dewa pejuang dan saingan Veles.
long_description.en: After his conversion Vladimir had the statues of Perun torn down, dragged, beaten and thrown into rivers; one source says the statue was cast into the Dnipro River and Saint Basil's Church was built on its site. The Church replaced the cult of Perun with that of Saint Elijah, who inherited all his qualities, yet the Lemkos still regard "May Perun strike you dead" as the most terrible curse. Today Perun is among the most revered gods of Slavic neopaganism (rodnovery), as a god of warriors and a rival of Veles.

claims.quote: In Slavic mythology, Perun (Cyrillic: Перун ) is the highest god of the pantheon and the god of sky, thunder, lightning, storms, rain, law, war, fertility and oak trees.

statement.id: Dalam mitologi Slavia, Perun (Перун) adalah dewa tertinggi dalam jajaran dewa, dewa langit, guruh, petir, badai, hujan, hukum, perang, kesuburan, dan pohon ek.
statement.en: In Slavic mythology, Perun (Перун) is the highest god of the pantheon and god of sky, thunder, lightning, storms, rain, law, war, fertility and oak trees.

claims.quote: His other attributes were fire, mountains, wind, iris, eagle, firmament ... horses and carts, and weapons (hammer, axe (Axe of Perun), and arrow).

statement.id: Atribut lain Perun adalah api, gunung, angin, bunga iris, elang, cakrawala, kuda dan kereta, serta senjata berupa palu, kapak (Kapak Perun), dan anak panah.
statement.en: His other attributes were fire, mountains, wind, iris, eagle, firmament, horses and carts, and weapons: hammer, axe (Axe of Perun) and arrow.

claims.quote: The supreme god in the Kievan Rus' during the 9th-10th centuries, Perun was first associated with weapons made of stone and later with those of metal.

statement.id: Sebagai dewa tertinggi di Rus Kiev pada abad ke-9 sampai ke-10, Perun mula-mula dikaitkan dengan senjata dari batu, kemudian dengan senjata logam.
statement.en: The supreme god in Kievan Rus in the 9th-10th centuries, Perun was first associated with stone weapons and later with metal ones.

claims.quote: To this day, the word perun in a number of Slavic languages means "thunder," or "lightning bolt".

statement.id: Hingga kini, dalam sejumlah bahasa Slavia kata perun berarti "guruh" atau "sambaran petir".
statement.en: To this day, in a number of Slavic languages the word perun means "thunder" or "lightning bolt".

claims.quote: As early as the 6th century, he was mentioned in De Bello Gothico, a historical source written by the Eastern Roman historian Procopius.

statement.id: Sejak abad ke-6 ia sudah disebut dalam De Bello Gothico, sumber sejarah karya sejarawan Romawi Timur Procopius.
statement.en: As early as the 6th century he was mentioned in De Bello Gothico, a historical source by the Eastern Roman historian Procopius.

claims.quote: In 980, when prince Vladimir the Great came to the throne of Kiev, he erected statues of five pagan gods in front of his palace which he soon thereafter discarded after his Christianization in 988. Perun was chief among these, represented with a silver head and a golden moustache.

statement.id: Pada tahun 980, ketika pangeran Vladimir Agung naik takhta di Kiev, ia mendirikan arca lima dewa pagan di depan istananya, yang kemudian ia singkirkan setelah masuk Kristen pada 988; Perun adalah yang utama, digambarkan berkepala perak dan berkumis emas.
statement.en: In 980, when Prince Vladimir the Great took the throne of Kiev, he erected statues of five pagan gods before his palace, discarding them after his Christianization in 988; Perun was chief among them, with a silver head and a golden moustache.

claims.quote: Perun is strongly correlated with the near-identical Perkūnas/Pērkons from Baltic mythology, suggesting either a common derivative of the Proto-Indo European thunder god

statement.id: Perun sangat berkaitan dengan Perkūnas/Pērkons yang hampir identik dari mitologi Baltik, yang menunjukkan asal bersama dari dewa guruh Proto-Indo-Eropa atau peminjaman.
statement.en: Perun is strongly correlated with the near-identical Perkūnas/Pērkons of Baltic mythology, suggesting a common Proto-Indo-European thunder god origin or borrowing.

claims.quote: The root *perkwu originally probably meant oak, but in Proto-Slavic this evolved into *per- meaning "to strike, to slay".

statement.id: Akar *perkwu semula mungkin berarti pohon ek, tetapi dalam bahasa Proto-Slavia berkembang menjadi *per- yang berarti "memukul, membunuh".
statement.en: The root *perkwu probably first meant oak, but in Proto-Slavic it became *per-, meaning "to strike, to slay".

claims.quote: Perun's lightning bolts were believed to be stones and stone arrows. According to folk beliefs, fulgurites, belemnites, and sometimes even the remains of prehistoric stone tools found in the ground are remains of these weapons.

statement.id: Kilat Perun dipercaya berupa batu dan anak panah batu; menurut kepercayaan rakyat, fulgurit, belemnit, dan kadang perkakas batu prasejarah yang ditemukan di tanah adalah sisa senjata itu.
statement.en: Perun's lightning bolts were believed to be stones and stone arrows; folk belief held fulgurites, belemnites and sometimes prehistoric stone tools found in the ground to be remains of these weapons.

claims.quote: The weapons of Perun protected against bad luck, evil magic, disease, and – naturally enough – lightning itself.

statement.id: Senjata Perun melindungi dari nasib buruk, sihir jahat, penyakit, dan juga dari petir itu sendiri.
statement.en: The weapons of Perun protected against bad luck, evil magic, disease and lightning itself.

claims.quote: it can also be shown that Perun was married to the Sun. He, however, shared his wife with his enemy Veles, as each night the Sun was thought of as diving behind the horizon and into the underworld, the realm of the dead over which Veles ruled.

statement.id: Perun dapat ditunjukkan menikahi Matahari, tetapi ia berbagi istri dengan musuhnya Veles, karena setiap malam Matahari dianggap terbenam ke dunia bawah, alam orang mati yang dikuasai Veles.
statement.en: Perun can be shown to have been married to the Sun, but he shared his wife with his enemy Veles, as each night the Sun was thought to dive into the underworld, the realm of the dead ruled by Veles.

claims.quote: Shrines of Perun were located either on top of mountains or hills, or in sacred groves underneath ancient oaks. These were general places of worship and sacrifices (with a bull, an ox, a ram, and eggs).

statement.id: Tempat pemujaan Perun berada di puncak gunung atau bukit, atau di hutan keramat di bawah pohon ek tua; di sana dilakukan ibadah dan persembahan berupa banteng, sapi, domba jantan, dan telur.
statement.en: Perun's shrines stood on mountain tops or hills, or in sacred groves under ancient oaks, as places of worship and sacrifice (a bull, an ox, a ram and eggs).

claims.quote: In addition to the tree association, Perun had a day association (Thursday) as well as the material association (tin).

statement.id: Selain pohon, Perun juga dikaitkan dengan satu hari, yaitu Kamis (Thursday), dan dengan satu bahan, yaitu timah.
statement.en: Besides the tree, Perun was associated with a day (Thursday) and a material (tin).

claims.quote: He ordered that the statues of Perun which he himself had erected formerly, be dethroned, torn down with great dishonor and dragged through the streets as they were beaten with sticks. The idols were then cast into rivers and not permitted to land on the shore.

statement.id: Ia memerintahkan agar arca-arca Perun yang dulu didirikannya sendiri dirobohkan dengan hina dan diseret di jalan sambil dipukuli tongkat, lalu dibuang ke sungai dan tidak dibiarkan terdampar di tepi.
statement.en: He ordered the statues of Perun he had once erected to be torn down in disgrace and dragged through the streets while beaten with sticks, then cast into rivers and not allowed to land on the shore.

claims.quote: Perun is one of the most revered gods in Slavic neopaganism (rodnovery). He is considered a thunderer, the god of warriors, and a rival of Veles, also embodying spring thunderstorms that fertilize the earth.

statement.id: Perun adalah salah satu dewa yang paling dihormati dalam neopaganisme Slavia (rodnovery); ia dianggap dewa guruh, dewa para pejuang, dan saingan Veles, serta perwujudan badai musim semi yang menyuburkan bumi.
statement.en: Perun is one of the most revered gods of Slavic neopaganism (rodnovery), seen as a thunderer, god of warriors and rival of Veles, embodying spring storms that fertilize the earth.

claims.quote: The Baltic tribes had a widespread cult of the thunderer Perkunas, one of the main deities of the Baltic pantheon. With Perun, this deity also shares common attributes (amulets in the form of an axe, a fiery four-pointed symbol, oak as the main tree)
claims.locator: The cult of Perun among neighboring tribes

statement.id: Suku-suku Baltik memuja dewa guruh Perkunas, salah satu dewa utama mereka, yang memiliki atribut sama dengan Perun: jimat berbentuk kapak, simbol api berujung empat, dan pohon ek sebagai pohon utama.
statement.en: The Baltic tribes widely worshipped the thunderer Perkunas, a main Baltic deity sharing attributes with Perun: axe amulets, a fiery four-pointed symbol and the oak as chief tree.

claims.quote: Among South Slavs, a mountain plant Iris germanica is known in folklore as perunika ("Perun's plant") and sometimes also as bogisha ("god's plant"), and was believed to grow from ground that had been struck by lightning.

statement.id: Di kalangan Slavia Selatan, tanaman gunung Iris germanica dikenal dalam cerita rakyat sebagai perunika ("tanaman Perun") dan kadang bogisha ("tanaman dewa"), dan dipercaya tumbuh dari tanah yang tersambar petir.
statement.en: Among South Slavs the mountain plant Iris germanica is known in folklore as perunika ("Perun's plant") and sometimes bogisha ("god's plant"), believed to grow from ground struck by lightning.

claims.quote: The Bulgarian and Macedonian people believe that the name of the Bulgarian mountain Pirin, one of the highest mountains of the Balkan Peninsula, was named after Perun.

statement.id: Orang Bulgaria dan Makedonia percaya bahwa Pirin, salah satu gunung tertinggi di Semenanjung Balkan, dinamai menurut Perun.
statement.en: Bulgarians and Macedonians believe the Bulgarian mountain Pirin, one of the highest in the Balkan Peninsula, was named after Perun.

claims.quote: Perun. One of the principal deities in eastern and northern Slavic mythology. In pre-Christian Kyivan Rus’ this was the chief god—the god of thunder, lightning, and rain, the ruler of the heavens, and, later, the god of war.

statement.id: Perun adalah salah satu dewa utama dalam mitologi Slavia timur dan utara; di Rus Kyiv sebelum Kristen ia dewa tertinggi, dewa guruh, kilat, dan hujan, penguasa langit, dan kemudian dewa perang.
statement.en: Perun is one of the principal deities of eastern and northern Slavic mythology; in pre-Christian Kyivan Rus he was the chief god, god of thunder, lightning and rain, ruler of the heavens and later god of war.

claims.quote: In 980 a wooden statue of Perun with a silver head and golden moustache stood on Perun Hill in Kyiv. Perun's feast, celebrated with sacrifices, took place in July.

statement.id: Pada tahun 980 arca kayu Perun berkepala perak dan berkumis emas berdiri di Bukit Perun di Kyiv; hari raya Perun dirayakan dengan persembahan pada bulan Juli.
statement.en: In 980 a wooden statue of Perun with a silver head and golden moustache stood on Perun Hill in Kyiv; his feast, with sacrifices, took place in July.

claims.quote: After adopting Christianity Prince Volodymyr the Great ordered Perun's statue to be cast into the Dnipro River and on its site built Saint Basil's Church.

statement.id: Setelah memeluk Kristen, Pangeran Volodymyr (Vladimir) Agung memerintahkan arca Perun dilempar ke Sungai Dnipro dan membangun Gereja Santo Basil di tempatnya.
statement.en: After adopting Christianity, Prince Volodymyr the Great had Perun's statue cast into the Dnipro River and built Saint Basil's Church on its site.

claims.quote: The Christian church replaced the cult of Perun with the cult of Saint Elijah (feast day: 2 August, or 20 July OS), to whom all of Perun's qualities were transferred.

statement.id: Gereja Kristen menggantikan pemujaan Perun dengan pemujaan Santo Elia, yang menerima semua sifat Perun.
statement.en: The Christian church replaced the cult of Perun with that of Saint Elijah, to whom all of Perun's qualities were transferred.

claims.quote: The Lemkos still consider the expression ‘May Perun strike you dead’ as the most terrible curse.

statement.id: Orang Lemko masih menganggap ungkapan "Semoga Perun menyambarmu mati" sebagai kutukan paling mengerikan.
statement.en: The Lemkos still regard the expression "May Perun strike you dead" as the most terrible curse.

claims.quote: The author analyses Perun, a supreme Storm-God in Old-Slavic pagan religion and mythology, which is correlated to rock, thunder, lightning and rain, war and justice.

statement.id: Penulis menganalisis Perun sebagai dewa badai tertinggi dalam agama dan mitologi pagan Slavia Kuno, yang berkaitan dengan batu, guruh, kilat, hujan, perang, dan keadilan.
statement.en: The author analyses Perun as a supreme storm god of Old Slavic pagan religion and mythology, correlated with rock, thunder, lightning, rain, war and justice.

claims.quote: For more than a century, scholars of Slavic mythology have adopted the assumption connecting the German iris (Iris germanica) plant and the cult of the god Perun.

statement.id: Selama lebih dari seabad, para ahli mitologi Slavia menerima anggapan yang menghubungkan tanaman iris Jerman (Iris germanica) dengan pemujaan dewa Perun.
statement.en: For more than a century, scholars of Slavic mythology have assumed a connection between the German iris (Iris germanica) and the cult of Perun.

claims.quote: the author concludes that there are no grounds for linking the plant to the cult of Perun, the god of thunder. The motivation for the name “perunika” comes from its dominant feather-like (perasti) leaves

statement.id: Penulis menyimpulkan tidak ada dasar untuk mengaitkan tanaman itu dengan pemujaan Perun, dewa guruh; nama "perunika" berasal dari daunnya yang mirip bulu (perasti).
statement.en: The author concludes there are no grounds for linking the plant to the cult of Perun, the thunder god; the name "perunika" comes from its feather-like (perasti) leaves.

claims.quote: Perun was worshipped by the Varangian (Scandinavian) warriors hired by Oleg and Igor during the campaigns against Byzantium ... It is likely that the purely Slavic god Perun replaced for them the Scandinavian Thor, also the thunderer.
claims.locator: The cult of Perun among neighboring tribes

statement.id: Perun dipuja para prajurit Varangia (Skandinavia) yang disewa Oleg dan Igor dalam kampanye melawan Bizantium; kemungkinan besar bagi mereka Perun menggantikan Thor dari Skandinavia, yang juga dewa guruh.
statement.en: Perun was worshipped by the Varangian (Scandinavian) warriors hired by Oleg and Igor against Byzantium; for them the purely Slavic Perun likely replaced the Scandinavian Thor, also a thunderer.

claims.quote: ペルーン（ウクライナ語 / キリル表記：Перун、ラテン表記：Perun）またはペルンは、スラヴ神話の主神であり、雷神。ロシア語ではほかにピィエルン (Pyerun)、またポーランド語ではピョルンまたはピオルン (Piorun)

statement.id: Perun (Перун) adalah dewa utama mitologi Slavia dan dewa guruh; dalam bahasa Rusia ia juga disebut Pyerun, dan dalam bahasa Polandia Piorun.
statement.en: Perun (Перун) is the chief god of Slavic mythology and a thunder god; in Russian he is also called Pyerun, and in Polish Piorun.

claims.quote: 類似する多くの雷神と同じように、髭を生やした中年男性の姿をしている。 石臼に乗って空を飛びながら稲妻を放ち雷鳴を轟かせる。

statement.id: Seperti banyak dewa guruh lain, ia berwujud lelaki paruh baya berjanggut; ia terbang di atas batu gilingan sambil melepaskan kilat dan guruh.
statement.en: Like many thunder gods he has the form of a bearded middle-aged man; he flies on a millstone, hurling lightning and thunder.

claims.quote: The Finnic peoples had a deity Ukko, which had similar functions and attributes with the Slavic and Baltic deities.
claims.locator: The cult of Perun among neighboring tribes

statement.id: Bangsa-bangsa Finnik memiliki dewa Ukko dengan fungsi dan atribut yang mirip dengan dewa Slavia dan Baltik.

summary.id: Satu sumber: bunga iris disebut perunika ("tanaman Perun") dan dipercaya tumbuh di tanah bekas sambaran petir; para ahli lama mengaitkannya dengan pemujaan Perun.
summary.en: One source: the iris is called perunika ("Perun's plant") and was believed to grow where lightning struck; scholars long linked it with Perun's cult.
